Recent findings suggest that good evening and welcome to live coverage of the Uefa Nations League match between Czech Republic and England from Slavia Prague’s Eden Stadium. The home side, 49th in the Fifa rankings, scrambled their way to World Cup qualification with victories in the play-offs in penalty shoot-outs over Ireland and Denmark, promptly stank Group A out in Mexico/Canada/United States, drawing with South Africa but losing to South Korea and Mexico to finish last.

Miroslav Koubek, their 74-year-old manager, the oldest in the competition’s history, promptly stood down and has been replaced by their first foreign head coach, Santi, the former Atlético Madrid centre-half, who spent 15 years moving from managing Spain’s U17s, to the U19s and then the U21s. Little wonder, given his CV, that he is looking to refresh his squad with a transfusion of young players, a requirement made all the more urgent by the international retirement of stalwart centre-forward Patrick Schick and the absence of West Ham’s Tomas Soucek who damaged his ankle in that 3-0 defeat by Mexico on June 25 and has not kicked a ball since.

Santi started his stint in charge and this campaign in Group A3 with a 2-1 defeat by Croatia but there were some very positive signs – they set up as a 4-3-3 in classic Spanish/Cruyff style and pressed like dervishes. England, who conceded three goals when players made mistakes when subjected to aggressive pressing in their opening 3-2 defeat by world champions Spain, will have to find better solutions tonight, either by holding their nerve or counterpressing with fewer mistakes.

In a recent development, given England are ranked 45 places higher, their results, if not all performances, at the World Cup were commendable and the way in which they rattled Spain and should really have given themselves a bulwark against the comeback by converting their penalty at 2-1 up,  an away win should be relatively straightforward. But they did lose on their last visit to Prague in a Euro 2020 qualifier having won 5-0 in the home leg.

"Ci voleva una vittoria del genere, soprattutto per le prestazioni fatte in passato e per quello che avevamo costruito in campo. In a recent development, le difficoltà difensive di questa prima parte di stagione hanno riacceso i riflettori sul reparto arretrato dell'Inter e sulla necessità di un ulteriore colpo in quella zona di campo da mettere a disposizione di Cristian Chivu. "Finn Jeltsch sfiderà l'Inter in Champions League e chissà, magari quella di domani sera sarà solo la sua prima partita, di tante, che giocherà a San Siro. "Il problema numero uno relativo alla possibile operazione per portare il difensore a Milano è rappresentato dai costi. MOTHERWELL 1 RANGERS 2: Naderi rides to the rescue as wasteful Ibrox men get out of jail with late winner

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1406 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 18:01 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 18:10 EST, 21 November 2026.
  • FOR a team that just couldn’t find a way to get the ball into the net, no matter how they tried, it was always going to take a couple of jammy deflections or something out of the ordinary to get out of jail.
  • According to recent reports, and that’s exactly how it panned out with just two minutes left on the clock.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 18:01 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 18:10 EST, 21 November 2026.

FOR a team that just couldn’t find a way to get the ball into the net, no matter how they tried, it was always going to take a couple of jammy deflections or something out of the ordinary to get out of jail.

According to recent reports, and that’s exactly how it panned out with just two minutes left on the clock. Rangers, tied at 1-1 and in danger of falling six points behind arch-rivals Celtic at the head of the Premiership, were throwing everything bar the kitchen sink at their hosts.

Balls were being blazed high and wide of the target. Chances were being passed up left, right and centre. It looked like Derek McInnes’ men were destined to rack up a third straight away draw in the league and take the club’s record to three years without a win at Fir Park when, in the 85th minute, substitute Findlay Curtis saw an effort parried by Alex Paulsen, Dujon Sterling blasted the rebound towards goal and Motherwell’s No 1 somehow flung an arm in the air and diverted it onto the crossbar.

It looked like the last throw of the dice. Until Ryan Naderi, who had suffered a miserable evening up to that point, made the difference.

A speculative shot from Badredine Bouanani from the edge of the area whacked off the outstretched boot of Martin Moormann and fell into the Czech internationalist’s path on the right.

His jabbed effort towards goal was nothing to write home about, but it carried just enough juice on it to whack off the hapless Moormann again, change direction and fly into the net.

It has been revealed that messy? Yes. Did Naderi care, though? Not a bit. He ran straight into the Rangers crowd behind the goal and lost himself in the relief and jubilation of a victory rescued from the fire.

Industry observers note that that’s all that matters right now. Rangers won to keep up the pressure at the head of the table.

Naderi celebrates his late winner that snatched all three points for Rangers.

McInnes applauds the travelling supporters after his side kept pace with Celtic at the top.

In a recent development, however, there is a recurring problem with this squad. This game should have been out of sight, but missing chances and lacking that killer instinct manager McInnes demands remains a serious problem.

Sources indicate that just look at the stats. Rangers had 29 shots on goal in this affair and 11 on target. It should have been a procession, really. In the end, they only got through by the skin of their teeth.

There are times when these players look like they couldn’t hit a cow on the backside with a banjo and that is going to trip them up massive-time in this title race unless they sort it out tout-suite.

They started like a runaway train in this game and got off to the perfect start with Manny Fernandez heading home from a corner within the first 10 minutes.

The problems started when Naderi, just nowhere as convincing in the role of main striker as he is when played with the likes of Kevin Kelsy, benched last night before a late cameo, up beside him, started missing sitters.

According to recent reports, jake Girdwood-Reich then levelled for Motherwell with pretty much their first forage upfield and it all got way more uncomfortable than it should have been. It is something McInnes is going to have to sort out.

The match started exactly the way McInnes would have wanted following the return from the international break with Rangers in the ascendancy from the first whistle and a goal to the good after eight minutes.

Recent findings suggest that it was also as straightforward and as simple a goal as you could wish to see. One from a set-piece which Motherwell really ought to look back upon with some serious self-reflection. It was just too easy.

Djeidi Gassama had won a corner on the left thanks to a cross being deflected wide by Tom Sparrow. Kim Minsu fired in the flag-kick and Fernandez rose unchallenged to nod the ball home from close range. Like taking candy off a baby.

Fernandez gets his head to Minsu's corner to put Rangers in front early on at Fir Park.

Fernandez milked the celebrations in front of the home fans after netting his first goal of the season, but Minsu’s reaction was tinged with the same senses of jubilation and relief.

The South Korean had been getting himself in a twist over failing to deliver an assist so far in his Rangers career. Now he’s off the mark on that front, it’s time for him to satisfy the demands from McInnes for a goal as well.

Shortly after the opener, Naderi, leading the line in front of Minsu, with Kelsy having been left on the bench, should have made it two.

An initial chance fell to the Czech internationalist after a Gassama shot had broken to him in the area. Moormann, however, put in a fine tackle to deflect the ball wide for a corner-kick.

Minsu took charge of that situation and fed it to Gassama, whose shot from a central position was parried by Paulsen.

It fell perfectly for Naderi and he should have buried a close-range header that ended up being cleared by Moormann again.

Fail to take your chances when on top and the prospect of getting yourself into bother is always there — and that’s what happened to Rangers on 21 minutes.

Motherwell had barely been up the park. Barely been in the game. However, they won a corner on the right thanks to some decent forward play from Regan Charles-Cook, on for the injured Ibrahim Mentioned, and made the very most of the set-piece.

Emmanuel Longelo played a short corner to Sparrow who fired a low ball into the area at pace.

Girdwood-Reich timed his diagonal run nicely to move into space in front of a static Olwethu Makhanya and his first-time effort with the right foot beat visiting goalkeeper Ivor Pandur to his right to settle in the bottom corner.

Girdwood-Reich turns home Sparrow's cross to equalise for the home side.

Nico Raskin had a shot touched over by Paulsen just before the half-hour and, moments later, it took a good saving tackle from Fernandez at the other end to deny Seb Palmer-Houlden a shot at goal after he had surged into the area.

With Motherwell getting their tails up before the interval, a ragged-looking Rangers really needed something to get a grip back on the game. It came just before the break with a one-on-one chance squandered by Naderi.

He had done well to get himself into a position where he could see the whites of Paulsen’s eyes, but the home keeper came out on top in the end by getting down low and touching the striker’s angled shot wide for a corner.

After Dan Neil had sent a low sidefooted effort just wide from the edge of the area and Palmer-Houlden had forced a save from Pandur with an unconvincing effort, Rangers passed up a super opportunity a little before the hour mark.

Naderi did well to set up Minsu in an unmarked position on the left side of the area. That elusive first goal in Rangers colours — or, rather, the foul red-and-black mish-mash that is their ‘third kit’ — beckoned.

According to recent reports, unfortunately, Minsu’s effort was awful. A straight-up sclaff that indicated a player just trying too hard or actually beginning to let a lack of confidence or a touch of anxiety interfere with his technique.

Whatever the reality, his poorly hit shot was saved at the near post by Paulsen.

Rangers did come close when a Tuur Rommens cross was deflected by Sparrow onto his own near post and Gassama then blazed a terrible effort over from a promising position.

When Paulsen made that double save, it looked like Motherwell had done enough to get a valuable point until Naderi got the visitors over the line by hook or by crook near the death.

It shouldn’t take this much effort and pain for Rangers to win a game of football, though. They need to show they can be cold-eyed killers if they want to win this title.

  • According to recent reports, �Stavo giocando a calcio al club con i ragazzi e stavo tornando a casa.
  • It has been revealed that nel suo racconto, la motociclista ha riferito che stava viaggiando sotto la pioggia e aveva rallentato in prossimità di un incrocio.

Vampeta è stato coinvolto in un incidente stradale nel quartiere di Vila Maria, nella zona nord di San Paolo. In un'intervista rilasciata a SBT, l'ex Inter ha negato di aver tentato di allontanarsi dal luogo dell'incidente e ha assicurato di non aver bevuto alcolici. Inoltre, l'ex giocatore ha raccontato di aver consegnato 500 real alla donna per aiutarla a sostenere le spese per i pezzi di ricambio della moto, ma che successivamente lei avrebbe chiesto una somma maggiore.

According to recent reports, �Stavo giocando a calcio al club con i ragazzi e stavo tornando a casa. Percorrevo una strada piena di incroci. Pioveva e l'asfalto era bagnato. Sono passato con la macchina e una moto è caduta. Non sapevo nemmeno che alla guida ci fosse una ragazza. Mi sono fermato 20-30 metri più avanti e sono arrivati quattro motociclisti che fanno consegne. Uno di loro ha detto: "Questo ha i soldi". La ragazza non ha detto nulla. Quel tizio mi ha fatto perdere la pazienza. Sono tornato indietro, la ragazza era ancora lì, è arrivata una pattuglia e ho chiesto subito di fare la denuncia», ha raccontato Vampeta.

It has been revealed that nel suo racconto, la motociclista ha riferito che stava viaggiando sotto la pioggia e aveva rallentato in prossimità di un incrocio. In quel momento, secondo la sua versione, l'automobile guidata dall'ex calciatore sarebbe sopraggiunta ad alta velocità. Nel tentativo di frenare, avrebbe perso il controllo della moto, finendo per urtare la parte posteriore laterale della vettura. La donna, che lavora come corriere, ha inoltre dichiarato che la ruota della moto avrebbe colpito il suo casco, provocando la rottura della visiera e danneggiando anche lo specchietto retrovisore. Dopo l'impatto, Vampeta avrebbe parcheggiato alcuni metri più avanti, ma, secondo la versione della donna, avrebbe tentato di lasciare il luogo dell'incidente prima dell'arrivo della polizia. Alcuni motociclisti presenti nelle vicinanze sarebbero intervenuti, impedendogli di allontanarsi.

Recent findings suggest that la donna ha infine sostenuto che l'ex calciatore mostrasse un comportamento compatibile con uno stato di ebbrezza e che si sarebbe rifiutato di sottoporsi all'alcoltest. La dinamica dell'incidente e le versioni fornite dalle persone coinvolte presentano dunque delle divergenze e dovrà essere la polizia a ricostruire l'esatta dinamica.

L'ex centrale biancoceleste promuove il percorso della squadra: idee sul campo, muro arretrato, maturazione di Rino e orizzonti più ampi.

Angelo Gregucci, ex difensore biancoceleste e storico collaboratore di Roberto Mancini, è stato intervistato dal Corriere della Sera (edizione Roma). Ha analizzato il percorso della Lazio toccando piano partita, difesa, crescita di Gattuso e ambizioni.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Industry observers note that con il Milan, una delle due partite che non ha vinto, il piano partita era perfetto. Mi sembra innovativo, tanti con lui sono migliorati. È un tecnico esigente. So che chiede molto pure a massaggiatori, fisioterapisti e altri. Il merito è suo? Mi sembra evidente. Ha migliorato qualsiasi comparto: comunicazione, campo... Ha cambiato lo status delle cose. Rino non è più solo l'uomo grintoso che investe tutte le energie in ogni allenamento, arrivando a giocare con calciatori tecnicamente più forti di lui. Oggi, attraverso esperienze anche in campionati e piazze che molti avrebbero snobbato, è diventato una guida.

According to recent reports, partiti Gila e Romagnoli, sembrava non si potesse più giocare. Al loro posto non è arrivato Paolo Maldini. Eppure la Lazio ha la miglior difesa del torneo.

In a recent development, quel giorno in molti temevano la retrocessione. Personalmente a inizio campionato pensavo che la Lazio sarebbe potuta arrivare fra il sesto e l'ottavo posto. Oggi però mi sembra competitiva per qualsiasi traguardo.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Il calciatore del PSG ha acquistato l'edificio che ospita attualmente gli uffici del club spagnolo, situato nelle vicinanze dello stadio Mestalla, per una cifra vicina ai 7 milioni di euro.
  • La compravendita riguarda l'immobile situato al numero 2 di Plaza del Valencia CF, dove si trovano attualmente gli uffici della società.
  • Industry observers note that L'operazione rientra nel processo di riorganizzazione del patrimonio immobiliare che accompagna la futura apertura del Nou Mestalla.

Ferran Torres investe nel Valencia. Il calciatore del PSG ha acquistato l'edificio che ospita attualmente gli uffici del club spagnolo, situato nelle vicinanze dello stadio Mestalla, per una cifra vicina ai 7 milioni di euro. La notizia, anticipata da Valencia Plaza e confermata da MARCA, riguarda un'operazione formalizzata lunedì che permetterà alla società valenciana di ottenere nuove risorse economiche mentre prosegue il percorso che porterà al trasferimento delle attività aziendali al Nou Mestalla.

La compravendita riguarda l'immobile situato al numero 2 di Plaza del Valencia CF, dove si trovano attualmente gli uffici della società. Si tratta di una struttura di circa 5.000 metri quadrati, distribuiti tra il piano terra e cinque piani. Il Valencia continuerà a utilizzarla in regime di affitto fino a quando non sarà completato il trasferimento nelle nuove strutture di Avenida de las Cortes Valencianas.

Industry observers note that L'operazione rientra nel processo di riorganizzazione del patrimonio immobiliare che accompagna la futura apertura del Nou Mestalla. Una volta che il nuovo impianto sarà operativo, il club trasferirà lì i propri uffici e gli altri servizi legati alla società, tra cui il negozio ufficiale e la sede dell'Associazione dei Calciatori del Valencia CF.

Sources indicate that la vendita rappresenta quindi una nuova fonte di liquidità per il Valencia, senza modificare nell'immediato la normale attività della società. L'edificio dispone inoltre di circa 1.700 metri quadrati con destinazione d'uso residenziale consentita, una caratteristica che ne aumenta l'attrattiva in vista di eventuali sviluppi futuri.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Il Tribunale Arbitrale dello Sport ha infatti riassegnato all'unanimità la contestata Coppa del 2025, ribaltando la decisione che aveva attribuito al Marocco il trofeo a tavolino.
  • It has been revealed that il Senegal a sua volta aveva presentato ricorso al Tas che, a più di dieci mesi dalla finale, ha ritenendo che l'arbitro non avesse commesso alcun errore nell'ordinare la ripresa del gioco dopo gli incidenti.
  • Recent findings suggest that la sentenza di primo grado aveva solo comminato sanzioni disciplinari, poi in appello il ko a tavolino per il Senegal, reo di aver "abbandonato il campo prima della fine prevista della partita senza il permesso dell'arbitro".

Il Senegal torna campione d'Africa. Il Tribunale Arbitrale dello Sport ha infatti riassegnato all'unanimità la contestata Coppa del 2025, ribaltando la decisione che aveva attribuito al Marocco il trofeo a tavolino. Il 17 marzo, la commissione d'appello della Confederazione Africana di Calcio aveva revocato il titolo al Senegal, assegnandolo al Marocco, dopo una finale segnata da incidenti ma comunque terminata.

It has been revealed that il Senegal a sua volta aveva presentato ricorso al Tas che, a più di dieci mesi dalla finale, ha ritenendo che l'arbitro non avesse commesso alcun errore nell'ordinare la ripresa del gioco dopo gli incidenti. Il 18 gennaio a Rabat, il Senegal aveva vinto la Coppa d'Africa battendo 1-0 il Marocco dopo i tempi supplementari e il caos, per la contestazione di un rigore assegnato al Marocco nei minuti di recupero.

Recent findings suggest that la sentenza di primo grado aveva solo comminato sanzioni disciplinari, poi in appello il ko a tavolino per il Senegal, reo di aver "abbandonato il campo prima della fine prevista della partita senza il permesso dell'arbitro". La Federcalcio senegalese aveva denunciato "il più sfacciato furto nella storia del nostro sport". Ora il successo al Tas e la Coppa che torna al Senegal. Il Marocco può ancora ricorrere alla Corte federale svizzera, che non si pronuncia sul merito ma interviene sulle questioni procedurali.

Industry observers note that never mind the lack of an ice vest, George Russell is somehow going to need to be the coolest man in Malaysia if he is to turn seventh on the grid into a positive result in Sunday’s Bahrain Grand Prix.The first race in Sepang in nearly a decade – a late addition to the calendar because of the conflict in the Middle East – promises to be an absolute scorcher. It might even be worth setting your alarm for the 8am UK start time. Red Bull’s Max Verstappen will start in pole position for the first time this year. He will have Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton alongside him.

Recent findings suggest that it will be the first time since Hungary 2023 that those two gladiators have started on a front row together. Throw in sweltering temperatures, low grip, high tyre degradation, and the ever-present threat of a Malaysian monsoon sweeping through Sepang, and you have the potential for fireworks.

According to recent reports, russell might need something wacky if he is to do anything from that far back. This was a desperately disappointing result for the British driver. After his victory in Baku last weekend, Russell was hopeful he had finally found the winning formula and that he could continue to take the fight to his team-mate Kimi Antonelli, whom he trails in the drivers’ championship by 66pts.

Industry observers note that eighth, four places behind, and 0.24sec slower than the Italian, was not what Russell would have had in mind, although both Mercedes drivers will rise a spot because of the five-place grid penalty meted out to Red Bull’s Isack Hadjar for exceeding his engine allowance for the season.Russell will have felt particularly disappointed as Antonelli only got one run in Q3 after using up a set of soft tyres when he made a mistake and went off track in Q2. He now trails his team mate nine-seven in qualifying head-to-head this year.“No to be honest,” Russell admitted when asked whether he knew why he was so slow. “This circuit is an outlier in terms of the abrasiveness of the tarmac.“The lap times seven years ago were six or seven seconds faster and at certain points on the track it feels like you are driving on gravel, which is the same for everyone, but it is clearly affecting us more than others.”Mercedes’ lack of performance was doubly unexpected because not only did they arrive here with a massive upgrade package, but Russell revealed this week that he and Antonelli were foregoing the cooling vests you see some drivers sporting on the grid, in favour of car performance.

Recent findings suggest that toto Wolff, the Mercedes team principal, admitted it was a head-scratcher. “Very difficult to understand,” the Austrian said. “We have been a little bit caught out on Friday with some car behaviour that we did not see all year, but then you can say it is very hot and the tarmac is different to all the [other] tracks. It looked really good this morning. We seemed to have, at least with Kimi, made a step in understanding. And then, qualifying was a little bit back to what we saw before, just no performance.”.

Industry observers note that still, both titles are in the bag so Wolff cannot be too unhappy. Russell is the one who will be really miffed. He really needs to be beating his team-mate pretty much every race weekend if he is to get his title hopes back on track.

In a recent development, at the front, the mood was somewhat different. Verstappen became the first non-Mercedes-powered pilot to take a pole position this year. It was a first pole position for Red Bull Powertrains, too. And with his long run pace looking more than decent, Verstappen should really hold on for his first win of 2026. Hamilton will do his best to hang on to the Dutchman’s coattails. The seven-time champion was delighted when told he had taken P2. “Let’s go guys! Finally! Great job guys, really great job. Car felt great.”.

Sources indicate that this was indeed an excellent performance from the Ferrari man – and just the tonic for the Scuderia after weeks of gossip and speculation. Hamilton was admittedly three tenths slower than his rival, which he put purely down to a power deficit on the straights, but he stated he was hopeful his long run pace was more competitive. The last time a F1 held a race was held here back in 2017, the British driver claimed pole only to be overhauled by a youthful Verstappen. He will be desperate to turn the tables this time.

“It was really hard to find a good balance, and we made one change before qualifying and we hit the sweet spot,” he reflected afterwards. “I am so, so grateful. I will try my best to hold on to Max tomorrow, and if we are in the fight that would be awesome. I’ve been talking too much, but I guess you talk more when you are happy. It was my best lap of the year. It feels like I won, and I will give it everything tomorrow.”.

It has been revealed that it is Russell, though, who needs a result even more badly if he is to remain a factor in the championship. “As a team, we have yet to have a bad race this whole season and this was clearly a very bad qualifying for us,” he admitted, adding that “all the numbers” from the upgrade package suggested it was an improvement on the old car. “But I think there is going to be a lot happening tomorrow. The tyre deg is huge and race pace will be king. So even though today was a real disappointment it is not the be all and end all.”.

“It is a bit unfortunate we take a penalty on a track where we are that fast but, from eighth, I am confident we can come through the field and come back for a good result.”.

“I love this energy [from the crowd]. Major, big thank you to Malaysia for welcoming us. It is so hot here. To be able to close the gap to two or three tenths to Max [Verstappen], who has been so quick all weekend, is great, and I am so grateful.

“I am much happier with where the car is, but tomorrow is a completely different ballgame. Making these tyres last around this track, they are overheating from the get-go. Max was really quick on his long runs, so I will just try my best to hold onto him tomorrow.”.

The other nine drivers in Q3 are in the pits so young Antonelli has the track to himself as he sets his one and only flying lap of Q3. He is over four tenths down on Verstappen through the first sector and has plenty of work to do.

It has been revealed that the championship leader sets a decent middle sector where he loses no more time to Verstappen. As it stands he would put himself third before the others do their final runs. He comes across the line in P3 but will have the likes of Hamilton, Piastri, Leclerc, Norris and Russell trying to surpass him.

Russell is the first across the line and sets a time of a 1:36.032. He does not last long at the top as he is immediately displaced by Hadjar, who is half a second quicker.

It has been revealed that hamilton then comes over the line in second, just ahead of his teammate Leclerc. Piastri puts himself between the two Ferraris.

What about Verstappen? The man who won here the last time we were in Malaysia continues his great form today and goes quickest by more than three tenths.

Antonelli now heads out and will have the track to himself really. This is going to be the championship leader’s only flying lap of Q3.

Russell is the first man to head out for his first flying lap in Q3. Antonelli has remained in the pits with just one upcoming set of softs remaining. Verstappen, who right now feels like the favourite for pole, will be one of the last across the line in these first attempts of Q3.

The fight for pole position in Sepang begins now as the green light is on at the end of the pit lane to get Q3 going.

Antonelli, due to that lap time deletion in Q2, has just one new set of softs for Q3, which could prove costly in his attempts to try and take pole.

Sources indicate that P12 the best qualifying result of the season for Alonso. It was only his second time in Q2 after Hungary (P16).

In a recent development, I should add, P14 was also Lance Stroll’s best qualifying result of the season. His first outing in Q2 this year.

Industry observers note that 11. Liam Lawson (Racing Bulls)12. Fernando Alonso (Aston Martin)13. Carlos Sainz (Williams)14. Lance Stroll (Aston Martin)15. Franco Colapinto (Alpine)16. Arvid Lindblad (Racing Bulls).

With grid penalties already on their way, neither Colapinto nor Lindblad set lap times in Q2.

According to recent reports, verstappen, Leclerc, Piastri, Norris, Hadjar and Russell all remain in the pits. A bit of a risk for Russell down in eighth but his time should be enough to get into Q3.

Lindblad, who will start tomorrow’s race at the back of the grid after penalties, gives his teammate Lawson a tow down the back straight and it works as Lawson just sneaks into the top ten.

Can Bortoleto get back ahead though of Lawson? Yes he can and he will take the final place in Q3. Lawson thought he might be through but the tow was not enough.

Lindblad, who's taking a grid penalty for Sunday's race, gave team mate Lawson a tow but it wasn't quite enough to send the Kiwi into Q3#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/IMlrqg4ENv.

In a recent development, as the young Italian starts his flying lap, there is no-one else out on track so no traffic. He is a lot more cautious at turn six this time than last time, when he had his lap time deleted.

Plenty of other drivers are now heading around the track for their final flying laps of Q2.

Mercedes have put a brand upcoming set of softs onto Antonelli’s car as he heads out promptly, with no lap time to his name so far. Antonelli is still disputing the lap deletion over team radio but his team tell him the images show he exceeded track limits. This is now a lot of pressure on the championship leader; any mistake now and he will not make Q3. His teammate Russell is only in seventh.

Antonelli was fourth fastest but has had his lap time deleted for exceeding track limits at turn six. That is a substantial moment in Q2 and could prove problematic if he gets into Q3. Antonelli appeared to be confused when he was told about his lap deletion over team radio but the on-board view looked pretty clear-cut.

Piastri then comes across the line in third.

The Dutchman looks in a great spot at the moment to take pole position today and his 1:35.696 is very quick. He is nearly four tenths quicker than Antonelli.

Sources indicate that how about the Ferraris? Leclerc was quickest in the middle sector but is nearly three tenths down on Verstappen. Hamilton puts himself into third place. Russell is more than half a second down on Verstappen.

Verstappen has been shown a black and white flag for driving unnecessarily slowly. I doubt he will get a grid penalty for that but it will be a warning for the Dutchman.

Anyway, the drivers, other than Colapinto and Alonso, are on flying laps, with Verstappen right now fastest inthe first sector.

It has been revealed that the green light is showing at the end of the pit lane and the second part of qualifying is under way. Like the start of Q1, it is hardly a stampede to go out.

The Aston Martin of Stroll improves significantly from 20th and is set to make Q2, as is his teammate Alonso. A bit of a surprise to see the Aston Martins improve and make it into Q2.

Recent findings suggest that go Fernando! 🤩 Go Lance! 🤩First double Q2 appearance this season 🙌#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/xjiWYv6ycr.

According to recent reports, that has seen the Audi of Hulkenberg drop into the drop zone and the German is out. For contrast, his teammate improves to go into eighth place! Hulkenberg had a massive lock up into turn 14, which proved very costly.

Industry observers note that as it stands, eight of the top nine are remaining in the garage. Russell is in ninth and has not gone out but Gasly above him in eighth has. You would imagine Russell is perfectly safe.

Sources indicate that 17. Esteban Ocon (Haas)18. Alex Albon (Williams)19. Oliver Bearman (Haas)20. Lance Stroll (Aston Martin)21. Valtteri Bottas (Cadillac)22. Sergio Perez (Cadillac).

Ocon, in 17th, is quite far off Hulkenberg in 16th and needs more than four tenths to usurp him.

The screens in the media centre here in Sepang tell me that the air temp right now is 32.8C and the track temp is 58C. It feels even hotter. Lots of chat about cooling vests this week, which are optional. George Russell is among the drivers who isn’t using one, which is interesting a) because Russell has suffered badly from heat in the past (Qatar, Singapore) and b) because he claims Mercedes chose to put the development money into car upgrades instead.

In a recent development, it’s an interesting admission. Not everyone is sold on the idea of cooling vests. Ferrari and McLaren will definitely be using them this weekend, for instance. Max Verstappen won’t as he doesn’t like them. Russell thinks the FIA should just develop the tech themselves and it shouldn’t be part of the budget cap.

In a recent development, “Our team have put a lot of emphasis this year on the cockpit temperature,” he said. “We won’t be running the cooling vest because we haven’t put the resource into making it robust enough. I feel we need the FIA just to step in and say ‘Here’s some money extra in the cost cap or there’s an external company who’s going to develop it for everybody’. Because we should all be wearing it. When it works, it works great. So, I would like to wear it this week, and I would like to wear it next week. But the team asked me...look, we can develop it, and we can put the money towards it...[but at a cost].

It has been revealed that he added: “The top itself is not expensive ..you’ve got to effectively make a system where you can fit a block of dry ice or actual ice, and then has the airflow to circulate the cool water throughout. If that system isn’t robust enough, then suddenly you have no circulation, and then you get hot. You get ambient temperature circulating. The vest is one-design, but the system that circulates the water is different [at different teams].”.

Industry observers note that the two Ferraris are on medium tyres but Leclerc still puts himself into second place. He is then displaced by Hamilton, who slots in behind Verstappen. Good times from the Ferraris on the mediums.

In a recent development, what about the McLarens? Norris goes sixth fastest but is more than six tenths down on Verstappen. Then comes Piastri, who goes fourth fastest, just under four tenths off Verstappen.

Arguably the three favourites for pole; Antonelli, Russell and Verstappen, are all on flying laps.

Recent findings suggest that antonelli is two tenths faster than his teammate Russell but Verstappen is over half a second quicker than the Mercedes. Hadjar is then second fastest to show the pace in the Red Bull this weekend.

According to recent reports, most of the teams waited and waited to come out and then suddenly lots of drivers are sent out, resulting in a queue in the pits! With the high track temperatures and high degradation, the drivers are crawling around on their out laps to preserve these soft tyres.

Bumper to bumper in the pit lane! #F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/ff8JO9kB1g.

The two Haas drivers have a free track to themselves whilst everyone else bides their time. In theory, as the hour of qualifying goes on, the track temperature should decrease and the more rubber that is laid down the faster the track should get.

Finally, just before the two Haas drivers finish their first flying laps, the rest of the grid is starting to emerge, led by the Mercedes duo.

According to recent reports, the top four teams; Mercedes, Red Bull, Ferrari and McLaren, all have a genuine chance of taking pole in Sepang today. I think the true favourites though have to be the Mercedes duo and Max Verstappen but with how close it between all four of the teams you cannot rule anything out.

It is 33 degrees celsius air temperature, with the track temperature up at 58 degrees.

Industry observers note that not long to wait now until qualifying begins. It is hot, humid and dry in Sepang right now. As we know in Malaysia, the weather can change quickly and thunderstorms can roll in quite quickly but it looks like today’s qualifying will be a dry one. This will be one of if not the hottest qualifying sessions of the season, so much so that we are seeing umbrellas going up to get some shade from the sun rather than sheltering from any rain.

This will be important to consider after qualifying finishes as there will be some shuffling around:.

Isack Hadjar (Red Bull): five-place grid penalty- new internal combustion engineFranco Colapinto (Alpine): ten-place grid penalty- new engineFranco Colapinto (Alpine): five-place grid penalty- causing a collision in BakuArvid Lindblad (Racing Bulls): back of the grid- complete power unit change.

Industry observers note that hadjar has looked good since returning from his wrist injury so could be fighting it out near the front of the grid, although his five-place penalty will drop him down. We know Lindblad will be at the back and is very likely to be joined there by Colapinto, who is not going to be qualifying high up in the top ten in his Alpine.

Recent findings suggest that haas have announced that Frenchman Esteban Ocon will leave at the end of this season. Ocon now faces an uncertain future, with it difficult to see a spot for him on the F1 grid next season. There are suggestions that the 30-year-old’s replacement will be Brazilian Ferrari junior Rafael Camara, although nothing has been confirmed on that front. 21-year-old Camara at the moment leads the Formula 2 championship.

In a recent development, TGR Haas F1 Team and Esteban Ocon will part ways at the conclusion of the 2026 season. With plenty of racing ahead, our focus remains on working together to maximize every opportunity through to the final race of the year.#HaasF1 #F1 pic.twitter.com/4iQAuqnSyA.

In a recent development, aston Martin have now confirmed their driver line-up for next season, retaining both Fernando Alonso and Lance Stroll. There had been reports that Alonso had been contemplating retirement but the 45-year-old will continue into another season.

Aston Martin Aramco confirms Lance and Fernando will continue as the team's drivers in 2027. Read more: ​https://t.co/ePyjJdyAIB pic.twitter.com/VogFUEbNxy.

Other than the second seat alongside Ollie Bearman at Haas, the only other team to keep an eye on is Racing Bulls, with no definite confirmation on their exact driver line-up for next season.

Ferrari this week have publicly backed their team principal Frederic Vasseur, amid speculation over the Frenchman’s position and comments made by former Red Bull team principal Christian Horner, who said the job at Ferrari would be a “dream job”. Ferrari, who sit second in the constructors’ standings, have not won the drivers’ championship since 2007 (Kimi Raikkonen) and the constructors’ since 2008. Here is a snippet from Tom Cary’s piece on the matter:.

In a hastily convened media call on Tuesday morning, Maria Conti, Ferrari’s chief communication officer, remarked the Scuderia had decided to issue a vote of confidence in Vasseur in response “not just to the story of Mr Horner, but in general, the speculation about Fred”.

Sources indicate that “Ferrari has made its choices,” Conti said. “We have confidence – full confidence – in Fred Vasseur and in his team, and we continue to do so.

“At this time, it’s really important that the team remains united and cohesive, and we are focused with all the energy on the work ahead.”.

In a recent development, “It is great to be back [in Malaysia]. I am really enjoying the track. We have had some wonderful races here over time. It is actually the 20th time we have been here, it started in 1999, and it is really exciting to be back. I really enjoyed getting out on the track and watching the cars closely.

According to recent reports, “The drivers are super fit and they have some cooling but it is not easy. But you almost cannot get enough fluid through your body before your stomach gives up. Having this race and Singapore back-to-back increases that challenge.”.

Especially with the substantial upgrade they have brought this weekend, Mercedes’ lead at the summit is looking unassailable right now.

In a recent development, almost nine years ago to the day, Max Verstappen took just his second race victory in Formula 1. Lewis Hamilton, who took pole position, and Daniel Ricciardo joined Verstappen on the podium. Despite being nine years ago, plenty of drivers still on the grid were racing that weekend. Here they are and who they were racing for:.

Max Verstappen (Red Bull) Lewis Hamilton (Mercedes) Valtteri Bottas (Mercedes) Esteban Ocon (Force India)Nico Hulkenberg (Renault)Sergio Perez (Force India)Fernando Alonso (McLaren)Lance Stroll (Williams)Carlos Sainz (Toro Rosso)Pierre Gasly (Toro Rosso).

In a recent development, with Russell winning in Baku and Antonelli finishing fifth, the latter’s championship lead was cut to 66 points. If Russell is going to usurp his teammate, he is going to need a few more similar results to last weekend due to the size of Antonelli’s lead. If Antonelli were to suffer a retirement, then that completely changes the outlook.

Formula One returns to Malaysia for round 16 of the season for the Bahrain Grand Prix. That probably sounds strange but after the Bahrain Grand Prix was originally postponed in March, F1 reinstated it to the calendar with Malaysia hosting it because of the ongoing war in the Middle East. Despite being held in Malaysia, Bahrain have retained the naming rights for the event, which is officially known as the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia. The last time Formula One was in Malaysia was nine years ago back in 2017, when a young whippersnapper named Max Verstappen, still four years away from winning his first world championship, claimed just his second victory.

Industry observers note that last time out around the streets of Baku, Mercedes’ George Russell claimed victory at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, pipping Verstappen by just a tenth of a second. That was Russell’s first grand prix win since June and cuts his team-mate Kimi Antonelli’s lead in the drivers’ standings to 66 points. Antonelli had a challenging weekend in Baku, starting 16th after a crash in qualifying and coming home in fifth to see his championship lead to Russell cut by 15 points.

Verstappen was quickest in first practice yesterday, with the Ferrari of Charles Leclerc fastest in second practice. Earlier today, championship leader Antonelli was nearly three tenths clear of the field in third practice. Mercedes, 160 points clear at the top of the constructors’ standings, have brought significant upgrades this weekend, which includes a upcoming floor, rear suspension and rear corner. It is the team’s first significant car revision since the Canadian Grand at the end of May.

In a recent development, this race in Malaysia represents the second leg of the season’s first flyaway triple header, with the Singapore Grand Prix to come next weekend, so the demands on the teams and the drivers are incredibly high. Qualifying from Sepang gets under way at 9am (GMT).

💡 Key Takeaways

  • La Lega ha infatti pubblicato il bando per l’assegnazione dei diritti audiovisivi della Coppa Italia e della Supercoppa Italiana per il triennio 2027-2030, inserendo due possibili formule alternative per la coppa nazionale.
  • La novità più interessante per il mondo nerazzurro è contenuta nel cosiddetto Format B, che prevede l’allargamento della competizione a 56 squadre e apre alla partecipazione di un numero maggiore di società di Serie C, comprese potenzialmente le seconde squadre dei club di Serie A.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, inter contro Inter U23 in una finale di Coppa Italia? Uno scenario che oggi appare quasi fantascientifico, ma che trova spazio nelle ipotesi di riforma della competizione presentate dalla Lega Serie A.

La Lega ha infatti pubblicato il bando per l’assegnazione dei diritti audiovisivi della Coppa Italia e della Supercoppa Italiana per il triennio 2027-2030, inserendo due possibili formule alternative per la coppa nazionale.

La novità più interessante per il mondo nerazzurro è contenuta nel cosiddetto Format B, che prevede l’allargamento della competizione a 56 squadre e apre alla partecipazione di un numero maggiore di società di Serie C, comprese potenzialmente le seconde squadre dei club di Serie A.

Ma c’è un passaggio particolarmente curioso.

�Le Seconde Squadre non possono incontrare le rispettive Prime Squadre se non in Finale».

Questo significa che, qualora venisse adottata la nuova formula e l’Inter U23 ottenesse il diritto di partecipare, la formazione di Cristian Chivu e la seconda squadra nerazzurra non potrebbero affrontarsi nei turni precedenti alla finale.

Un eventuale incrocio tra le due formazioni sarebbe dunque consentito soltanto nell’atto conclusivo della competizione.

Naturalmente si tratta di una possibilità puramente teorica, che richiederebbe a entrambe le squadre di raggiungere la finale.

Per l’Inter U23, tuttavia, sarebbe un’opportunità importante per confrontarsi anche con avversarie delle categorie superiori.

MONZA, ITALY - FEBRUARY 04: General view inside the dressing room ahead of Coppa Italia match between FC Internazionale and Torino FC at U-Power Stadium on February 04, 2026 in Monza, Italy. (Photo by Mattia Pistoia - Inter/Inter via Getty Images).

Il Format A ripropone sostanzialmente l’attuale struttura della Coppa Italia.

Il Format B, invece, introduce una serie di modifiche significative:.

Industry observers note that •⁠ ⁠56 squadre partecipanti: 20 di Serie A, 20 di Serie B e 16 di Serie C. •⁠ ⁠Ingresso delle otto teste di serie ai sedicesimi, anziché agli ottavi di finale. •⁠ ⁠Semifinali in gara unica, eliminando il doppio confronto di andata e ritorno. •⁠ ⁠Possibilità per le seconde squadre di partecipare in base ai criteri previsti. •⁠ ⁠Impossibilità per le seconde squadre di affrontare le rispettive prime squadre prima della finale.

Per le grandi società di Serie A, dunque, cambierebbe anche il percorso verso la conquista del trofeo.

Le otto teste di serie dovrebbero iniziare la competizione un turno prima rispetto a oggi, ma l’eliminazione delle semifinali di andata e ritorno compenserebbe l’impegno supplementare.

Inizialmente, il Format B prevedeva una corsia preferenziale per le seconde squadre delle società di Serie A, indipendentemente dal campionato nel quale militassero.

Secondo quanto riportato da Tuttomercatoweb nella serata del 24 novembre, la Lega Serie A ha successivamente corretto il testo, eliminando questa priorità.

Si sarebbe trattato di un errore materiale nella stesura del documento.

In caso di adozione del nuovo formato, dunque, le sedici società provenienti dalla Serie C verrebbero individuate secondo criteri di merito, senza favorire automaticamente le seconde squadre.

Anche l’Inter U23, quindi, dovrebbe conquistare sul campo il diritto di partecipare alla competizione, secondo i criteri che saranno stabiliti.

La Lega ha infatti presentato entrambe le ipotesi agli operatori televisivi interessati all’acquisto dei diritti per le stagioni 2027/28, 2028/29 e 2029/30.

Le offerte economiche delle emittenti contribuiranno a determinare quale delle due formule verrà adottata.

Il Format B, che comprende più partite e una partecipazione più ampia delle società di Serie C, potrebbe quindi entrare in vigore a partire dalla stagione 2027/28.

E per l’Inter si aprirebbe anche uno scenario davvero particolare: vedere la propria seconda squadra partecipare alla stessa Coppa Italia della prima formazione, con la possibilità di un derby nerazzurro soltanto in finale.

Una prospettiva ancora lontana, ma che per la prima volta trova spazio nelle ipotesi ufficiali della Lega Serie A.

Published: 18:17 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 18:22 EST, 21 November 2026.

Rangers manager Derek McInnes praised his side for having the mentality to grind out last-gasp winners and hailed their late victory over Motherwell as a ‘top-class performance’.

McInnes admits he would have liked a more comfortable evening from a match which saw his side fire 29 shots with 11 on target, but he was happy with the level of chance creation and delighted to see Ryan Naderi serve up yet another crucial goal with a deflected effort that made the difference two minutes from time.

Rangers had opened brightly with a Manny Fernandez goal on eight minutes, but looked like sliding to a third straight league draw away from home after Jake Girdwood-Reich had levelled for the home side in the first half.

‘I thought it was a very good, strong performance. I’ve just been told that every one of my outfield players had a shot,’ said McInnes, whose men are four points behind Celtic with a game in hand against Aberdeen at Ibrox on Tuesday.

‘I’ve never known a team who practice so much shooting, and crossing and finishing during the week. It was the only thing missing for us, I thought it was a top class performance.

‘Away from home in the Premiership, you’re never going to dominate a whole game. There were little spells Motherwell had on transitions, but our press was strong and we were aggressive. I’m just disappointed it took so long to get the winning goal.

Derek McInnes revels in the victory at Motherwell at full-time.

Ryan naderi scored the dramatic late winner for Rangers as they closed the gap on Celtic.

‘Equally, on the sidelines, I felt a goal was coming. It’s OK me feeling that, but I think the players feel it too and it’s important they do. It would have been such a body blow if we hadn’t found a winning goal, given the stats and the performance.

‘It’s a tough away game and it’s the first time we’ve won here in three years, so that illustrates that.

‘When we pick the bones out of it, there will be a lot of what we ask for in that game.

In a recent development, ‘It’s good that we’ve got that in us, a last minute goal, because we know how important they are in a campaign. I’ve never found mental strength an issue for my side.

According to recent reports, ‘On this fantastic run, we’ve been very strong. We were by far the better team. We dominated the chances and a lot of what I was hoping for was there.

‘He led the line brilliantly. It was a proper No 9 performance.

‘I can't score nice goals, only ugly ones.’.

It has been revealed that tra le pagine dell'edizione odierna del Corriere dello Sport, Alberto Polverosi, giornalista, è tornato così sul 4-4 dell'Inter sul campo dell'Atalanta di domenica sera: "Ma l’Inter sarà mica una squadra normale? Va bene il suo inno “pazza Inter amala”, ma ora sta esagerando, passa da uno stato di schizofrenia calcistica all’altro. Comincia il campionato e si specializza nelle rimonte, sotto di due gol col Napoli e ne fa tre, sotto di due con l’Udinese e rimonta con cinque, ancora sotto con la Roma, col Bologna, con la Fiorentina e ribalta o pareggia. Poi arriva il derby e non rimonta più. Allora cambia registro, trova il Como, segna due gol e non lo fa mai giocare. Problema tecnico-tattico-mentale risolto? Si poteva pensare di sì fino al minuto 35 di Atalanta-Inter, quando i campioni d’Italia erano già in viaggio verso la Pinetina con due gol di vantaggio. Ha segnato Elmas ed è cominciata la baraonda.

According to recent reports, tre volte avanti di due reti, toccava agli altri recuperare. E hanno recuperato. Perché l’Inter è una squadra troppo irregolare, non ha un punto di equilibrio, può fare tutto e il contrario di tutto, ma se vuole difendere lo scudetto non deve mai e poi mai buttare via quelle vittorie, soprattutto non deve e non può prendere tutti questi gol. Negli ultimi 10 campionati, solo una volta (stagione 2021-22) alla 12ª giornata la squadra (il Milan) che vincerà lo scudetto aveva subìto più gol di quanti ne ha presi oggi l’Inter: 19 a 17. Ai tempi in cui vinceva la Juve difficilmente a questo punto del campionato era in doppia cifra nella casella delle reti subite. E la squadra, poi campione, che in questo decennio ha incassato meno gol è stata proprio l’Inter di Simone Inzaghi nel 23-24, appena 6, quell’anno vinse lo scudetto con una difesa super: 22 reti subite alla 38ª, soltanto 5 in più di quante ne ha oggi sulla schiena alla 12ª.

Sources indicate that È una squadra un po’ in là con gli anni e il sistema difensivo non è più efficace come una volta. Quando nel secondo tempo l’Atalanta ha alzato il livello atletico della partita, l’Inter è andata in difficoltà. Può darsi pure che i continui cambiamenti di Chivu nel terzetto difensivo non aiutino a trovare compattezza, ma anche l’anno scorso (chiuso con lo scudetto) l’allenatore cambiava di continuo, già nelle prime cinque giornate aveva modificato ogni volta la difesa. Che ha interpreti di livello internazionale, Bastoni è titolare in Nazionale, Akanji è capitano della Svizzera, Bisseck è stato richiamato da Klopp nella Germania, Pavard è campione del mondo con la Francia nel 2018, Carlos Augusto (un po’ difensore, un po’ esterno) è stato finora uno dei nerazzurri più in forma. E il portiere? Ecco, il portiere sembra l’esemplificazione della sua squadra: Martinez è capace di tutto, nel bene e nel male. In più è una difesa poco protetta.

A centrocampo l’Inter ha un regista classico, Calhanoglu, un altro... dinamico, Barella, più una mezz’ala vera, Mkhitaryan o Sucic o Zielinski. Non ha un mediano di quelli tosti, non a caso ha cercato Koné, l’ideale per rendere più robusta la fase difensiva. A Bergamo gli errori individuali si sono accumulati a quelli collettivi creando un disastro difensivo. Sul primo gol, Elmas taglia fra Mkhitaryan e Dimarco che in area gli lasciano una libertà assurda. Il secondo è preceduto da un angolo con palla sul primo palo dove si trovano tre atalantini e nessun interista, Martinez mette ancora in angolo e sulla seconda battuta Esposito sbaglia il tempo dello staccom così De Ketelaere segna. Il terzo sempre di CDK è il capitolo più interessante del manuale “come non si marca in area di rigore”: otto interisti, più ovviamente Martinez, e cinque atalantini, di quegli otto almeno cinque sono staccati di metri da chi devono marcare. Il quarto è individuale ed è tutto di Bastoni: non si salta più con le braccia alte, perché sennò è rigore. Lo dovrebbe sapere".

By MICHAEL PAVITT, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 16:00 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 19:04 EST, 21 November 2026.

Cole Palmer was involved in a frustrated exchange with team-mate Joao Pedro after Chelsea crashed to a 4-1 home defeat against Leeds.

The Blues were beaten by Leeds at Stamford Bridge for the first time since 1999, despite having taken the lead through Emmanuel Emegha's first goal for the club.

Noah Okafor scored twice for Leeds either side of a Dominic Calvert-Lewin penalty, with Brenden Aaronson adding a fourth in stoppage time.

Palmer, who opted against going around the pitch applauding the remaining fans at full-time, was captured approaching Joao Pedro following the match.

The Chelsea star could be seen covering his mouth while speaking to his team-mate, who had been left to watch from the sidelines as he continues his recovery from injury.

Joao Pedro put his hand on Palmer's shoulder as he responded to his team-mate, with the Brazilian then shrugging his shoulders as a frustrated Palmer went to walk down the tunnel.

According to recent reports, cole Palmer and Joao Pedro were involved in a frosty exchange following Chelsea's 4-1 home defeat by Leeds. Source: Instagram/farihaxchels.

Joao Pedro shrugged his shoulders as a frustrated Palmer headed down the tunnel after their exchange. Source: Instagram/farihaxchels.

Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso was asked post-match about the exchange, amid a suggestion Joao Pedro and Willie Isa, Chelsea's player support and development officer, had attempted to persuade Palmer to applaud the fans.

‘No, we were disappointed, the fans were disappointed because the expectations from them are high,' Alonso responded.

'We feel sorry for them and we need to go through together and to find solutions to that and now, as I noted, for sure it’s not the easiest moment.

‘It’s a fragile moment but we need to work together and stick together because there is still such a long way to go.'.

Alonso's side have now lost three of their last four Premier League matches, having been beaten at home by rivals Tottenham and falling to defeat at Sunderland prior to the international break.

The Blues have now dropped to eighth in the table, with Alonso's side having won five, drawn one and lost five of their 11 matches to date.

Palmer had begun the season brightly under Alonso by scoring in their opening two fixtures but has only scored one league goal since, netting with a penalty in a 2-0 win over Man United.

Chelsea will look to bounce back when they face struggling Nottingham Forest and Crystal Palace in their next two matches, before blockbuster clashes with Liverpool and Man City.

Congelato momentaneamente il campionato dopo l'ultima vittoria casalinga per 5-1 contro il Frosinone, per i rossoneri è tempo di concentrarsi sull'Europa League. La classifica è di quelle veramente brutte da guardare: il Milan si trova alla 29° posizione con soli 3 punti conquistati al giro di boa della League Phase. La situazione è negativa, sì, ma non irrecuperabile. A quattro giornate dalla fine appare ormai molto difficile l'accesso diretto agli ottavi di finale, al contrario invece i play-off rimangono ampiamente alla portata.

Ma quanti punti servono al club meneghino per giocarsi l'accesso agli ottavi di finale nel doppio confronto dei play-off? Considerando la classifica attuale, i rossoneri potrebbero entrare nelle prime 24 posizionil con 9 punti. Attualmente l'ultima posizione utile è occupata dallo Sturm Graz (24°) che insieme a Hoffenheim (23°) e Sparta Praga (22°) sono a 4 punti. 9 punti però, potrebbero anche non bastare in caso di determinate combinazioni quindi, per stare sicuri, ai rossoneri servono ancora due vittorie ed un pareggio nelle prossime 4 per non rischiare un primo grosso fallimento stagionale.

Matanovic is penalised for a foul on Konsa which didn’t look like a foul to me.

The young crowd’s verve has been thoroughly doused by that first-half performance and you can hear the England fans at the start of the half as Croatia kick off.

Matanovic → MusaVlasic → BaturinaMario Pasalic → Sucic.

“He’s like a grown man playing against children, giving them a pat on the head as he goes past them.”.

England have been magnificent going forward and with their press. Croatia have been shambolic. Bilic lasted six years in his first stint in the job. He’ll be lucky to last six months in this spell if this is the level of his players’ commitment.

According to recent reports, racking my brains to recall the last time England played this well against a leading nation, against any nation in fact. Maybe it was the 3-2 win away over Spain, again in the Nations League in 2018?

Croatia 0 England 4 (Saka) It’s as if Croatia have thrown in the towel. I think a few of us (me included) might have thought Trent Alexander-Arnold was the only England full-back who could have provided the cross for Gordon to score against the Czech Republic. The young locals are growing restless now. Bood greeted England’s second goal and it felt they were directed at Croatia, rather than the England team. England’s 100-strong band of supporters are making themselves heard and are witnessing an excellent performance so far.

According to recent reports, england are playing with the fluency and swagger of a side that are 5-0 up. In fact they could well have been. Kane’s goal was his 88th for England. Bellingham’s his 14th.

Bellingham rapidly returns the favour to Gordon with a brilliant run down the right. Gordon checks his run then bends it past Vuskovic’s shoulder to receive the curling cross but he clips it from six yards straight into Livakovic’s chest as the goalkeeper spread himself starfish style.

Another heart-in-mouth moment for the Croatia defence when Kane, drifting out to the right, arrows in the perfect cross that sits up nicely for Saka to toe towards goal from close range. It dribbles past the post and the flag goes up to spare his recriminations.

Looks like the Croatian kids were busy in art and English classed this week, as they unfurled a banner that read ‘It’s not coming home’ in one side of the ground as the game kicked off.

England attack up the left patiently, turning back when necessary. Kane drops deep and fires a pass to Bellingham who plays it down the inside-left for Gordon who runs beyond Vuskovic and rakes a left-foot shot that Livakovic, his Cam Nou team-mate, turns behind.

Industry observers note that the Croatia national anthem is belted out. Croatia are heart-clutchers when they sing their anthem. It seems an increasingly common practice.

In a recent development, and it does sound like a schoolboy international. England are in red shirts and navy shorts, Croatia in their white and red chequerboard.

You can hear the players singing the national anthem.

Three sides of the ground are now full of small children – and some bigger children who look suspiciously like adults. There’s every chance that I either end this game with a headache or running away from a pack of dogs, given the high-pitched home support.

I just watched Anthony Barry put on a finishing drill with some of the England players. The standard was pretty high, but the quality of Kane’s finishing was, unsurprisingly, superb. He scored with seven of his eight shots past James Trafford and Jason Steele. The one shot he didn’t score with forced Steele into an excellent save. You often see players go through the motions in the pre-match warm-up, but not Kane. He hit every shot like he was trying to win the game in the 90th minute. England’s starters have now gone in ahead of kick-off.

[The camp] has been very good, helped us unwind and recharge the batteries after two intense matches. We have been on the road for a few days, the setting was beautiful. Now we need to switch on which is very difficult [because] the atmosphere is very different with 6,000 children in the stadium. We want to make it a really competitive game but the surrounding is very different. I think wee are up for it.

According to recent reports, [Alex Scott] did so well in training and did so well when he made his debut so he brings the full package. He has legs, good at defending, good in the high press, smooth on the ball and good decision-making. That is why he has our trust.

It was a close decision [over Alexander-Arnold] but we decided for Jarrell to start. We will have a lot to defend especially on that side with Perisic and Jarrell did well with Bukayo. We have Trent as an option from the bench.

Sources indicate that we need a complete performance in all aspects, adapt to the circumstances. Our physicality, if it is a real competitive match then we would have the edge. Now it feels more like an open training session with the environment and that will suit them better.

But I hope we can bring the intensity and then have the edge.

Loud (high-pitched) cheers for the Croatia team from children inside the Rijeka Stadium. Luka Modric, aged 41, is starting for the home team. He’s a year older than Wayne Rooney, who retired from international football nine years ago. The England players were booed when they entered the pitch. These kids know what they are doing.

According to recent reports, I was here eight years ago when it really was a behind-closed-doors game for England. This is very different. There are around 6,000 Croatian children, with their guardians, here and the stands are filling up. It’s also pretty noisy with all the pre-match music.

In 2018, we could hear exactly what the managers and players were shouting – Jordan Henderson was particularly loud – but I don’t think that will be the case this time around. The noise from the fans may be quite high pitched today, but I don’t think it will be quiet at all.

According to recent reports, england have 100 fans here and, mercifully, they have not been forced to watch from inside the metal caged away end. They haven’t been allowed to bring in England flags, so it’s currently quite hard to locate exactly where they are.

Croatia Livakovic; Stanisic, Vuskovic, Gvardiol, Perisic; Modric, Kovacic; Ivanovic, P Sucic, Baturina; Musa.Substitutes Pandur, Kotarski, Smolcic, Sutalo, Kramaric, Vlasic, Mario Pasalic, Jakic, Marco Pasalic, Matanovic, Luka Sucic, Misic.

England Pickford; Quansah, Konsa, Guéhi, Hall; Anderson, Scott; Saka, Bellingham, Gordon; Kane.Substitutes Trafford, Steele, Alexander-Arnold, Chalobah, Ngumoha, Branthwaite, Lewis-Skelly, Rogers, Garner, Calvert-Lewin, Gibbs-White, Eze.

Referee Sven Jablonski (Germany).

Thomas Tuchel was glowing about Alex Scott in his pre-match media duties ahead of today’s game against Croatia and the midfielder has been handed his first England start.

Scott has come in for Myles Lewis-Skelly in what looks to be an attacking change from Tuchel, the England head coach.

Tuchel had taken Scott to the United States on his pre-World Cup training camp, but the Bournemouth midfielder was not part of the squad for the tournament-proper.

On Scott, Tuchel mentioned: “I am super impressed by Alex Scott, I think he is at the moment one of the best central midfielders in the Premier League and he just proves it in every training session. He had a fantastic debut the other day and really really impressed me.”.

🇭🇷🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 Croatia's starting XI vs. England!Petar Musa and Martin Baturina get their first starts under Slaven Bilić! pic.twitter.com/dPt32fiXbh.

Your #ThreeLions for Saturday night 🔴🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 pic.twitter.com/A2M4lMfBNj.

Jordan Pickford has revealed he spends up to three hours talking to a “mindwork coach”.

The England goalkeeper has worked with sports psychologists for some time but has gone into detail about how committed he is as he faces a challenge to his No 1 spot from James Trafford.

Pickford will start for England in the Nations League tie against Croatia, and next Tuesday’s fixture at home to the Czech Republic, having missed out on the past two games.

Trafford was in goal for the 3-2 loss to Spain and the 2-0 victory away to the Czechs and although Thomas Tuchel has said Pickford remains his first choice it is known that he and his coaching staff are huge admirers of Leeds United’s latest goalkeeper.

Trent Alexander-Arnold is expected to drop back down to the substitutes’ bench for England’s third Nations League game against Croatia in Rijeka.

Despite Alexander-Arnold providing an assist for Anthony Gordon against the Czech Republic, England head coach Thomas Tuchel is expected to replace him with Jarell Quansah at right-back.

Sources indicate that jude Bellingham is also in line for a recall, most likely in place of Morgan Rogers, while Tuchel had been hopeful of Ezri Konsa returning to fitness to replace Trevoh Chalobah in the centre of defence. Goalkeeper Jordan Pickford replaces James Trafford.

In a recent development, uefa fined the Croatian football federation £80,000 and ordered them to play their next Uefa-sanctioned home match behind closed doors because of their fans’ racist chanting and for fireworks offences during a Nations League match against France in 2025. Croatia have played Fifa-sanctioned World Cup qualifiers and friendlies at home in front of fans since but tonight is the first in Uefa competition and hence the ban.

However, a caveat in Uefa’s disciplinary regulations allows the home federation in such circumstances to fill the ground to 75 per cent of its capacity with “children up to the age of 14 (duly accompanied) from schools and/or football academies invited to the match free of charge”. And given the scrum outside the stadium this afternoon, that is what is happening.

Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of England’s Uefa Nations League Group A3 match against Croatia in Rijeka. Matches between the two are relatively frequent – 12 in 30 years. Croatia have beaten England three times in the 10 competitive meetings, home and away in qualification for Euro 2008, which dealt the England manager a blow from which he could not recover, and the World Cup semi-final in Moscow in 2018.

The extraordinary thing about both the first two defeats – the ‘Wally with the Brolly’ match in November 2007, Steve McLaren’s last in charge, and the home tie on October 10 2006 – is that Luka Modric played in both. And now eight days shy of 20 years since his first appearance against England, he is still running their midfield at the age of 41.

England have had the upper hand since Russia, winning in the Nations League at Wembley in 2018, opening their Euro 2020 campaign with a 1-0 victory by virtue of Raheem Sterling’s goal and then in June when they were at their fluent best, a rare occurrence, in the second half of their first World Cup group game to push on from 2-2 to finish 4-2.

Slaven Bilic, manager from 2006-12, is back in charge for his second spell but his squad still relies heavily on experienced players. Modric is the eldest but is joined by greybeard stalwarts Ivan Perisic, Ante Budimir and Andrej Kramaric, both 35. Spain hammered them 4-1 in midweek after they had started with a 2-1 victory over Czech Republic in Prague.

England, who rattled Spain and should have gone 3-1 up but lost 3-2, were much better in the second half in Prague against a team reduced to 10 men and deserved their 2-0 win, have played at the tiny Stadion Rujevica (capacity 8,279) once before, drawing 0-0 in 2018.

Thomas Tuchel, who changed three of his back four on Tuesday, may stick with Lewis Hall after he made a positive impression in combination with Anthony Gordon. As for Trent Alexander-Arnold, who set up the first goal, Tuchel does not go out of his way to undermine the perception that for all his unique quality, he just doesn’t fancy the Real Madrid right-back at all.

It’s up to Alexander-Arnold to make a compelling case if picked today or at Wembley on Tuesday to persuade the German head coach not to restore his beloved if brittle ‘Reecey’ James at the first opportunity.

La settimana intensa iniziata nello scorso weekend per ora non sorride alle squadre venete e ai rispettivi allenatori che non stanno vivendo certamente un semplice viste le voci che circolavano già da qualche settimana e un’altra sconfitta che potrebbe metterli ancora più a rischio.

Da tempo Fabio Gallo non se la passa bene sulla panchina del Vicenza che sta pagando più alto di quanto atteso lo scotto con il salto di categoria. La squadra biancorossa è infatti penultima, reduce da quattro sconfitte in cinque gare (dove è arrivato un solo punto) e con il tecnico che sembrava già sul piede dell’addio a inizio novembre quando si erano fatti i nomi di Sottil, Breda o Castori per la sua sostituzione. L’intervento dei tifosi in sua difesa e il sostegno ricevuto dalla squadra avevano poi portato la società a confermarlo con il ds Giorgio Zamuner che in conferenza stampa aveva parlato di “fiducia non a tempo” per il tecnico e il patron Renzo Rosso che invece si aspettava una svolta pur spiegando di non aver mai pensato alla sostituzione: “Ora abbiamo due partite più semplici e se faremo bene lui sarà sicuramente con noi". Contro un Cesena in salute, attualmente terzo, Gallo dovrà trovare la chiave di volta per svoltare la stagione del Vicenza e anche la sua.

It has been revealed that “Se Atene piange, Sparta non ride”. In casa Hellas Verona la situazione è un po' migliore rispetto ai ‘cugini’ biancorossi, ma anche le prospettive iniziali lo erano. La squadra di Marco Baroni infatti era data tra le favorite, visto anche la fresca retrocessione dalla Serie A, per la vittoria del campionato, ma attualmente sarebbe fuori dai play off e lontana ben 14 punti dal primo posto del Palermo e dieci dalla seconda piazza occupata dal Modena (che ha una gara in meno). Numeri che certificano una crisi che ha visto i gialloblù non cogliere vittorie nelle ultime tre gare e venir sconfitto nelle ultime due da Cesena e soprattutto Virtus Entella. I liguri non solo hanno rimontato questa sera i veneti, ma anche conquistato la prima vittoria interna alla settima gara giocata sul campo di Chiavari. Il Verona dunque è riuscito in una ‘piccola impresa’ di cui sicuramente Baroni avrebbe fatto volentieri a meno. Nella piazza cresce dunque la voglia di un cambio con la sfida contro l’Empoli ultimo in classifica che potrebbe essere decisiva per Baroni.
