📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 01:43 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 01:45 EST, 22 November 2026.

All eyes will be on Manchester United's latest head coach Mauricio Pochettino when they take on Liverpool at Anfield this afternoon.

Recent findings suggest that liverpool manager Andoni Iraola has freshened up the squad since joining in the summer, including the £123million purchase of Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain, while blending in young emerging talent. They have made a solid start across all four competitions, knocking Chelsea out of the League Cup on penalties, and they currently sit in fourth place in the Premier League.

In a recent development, united have had a dire start to the season, with only one win in 10 games leading to the axeing of head coach Michael Carrick. Will his replacement be able to save the season and galvanise a group of talented but dispirited players?

So, who from United’s struggling side have done enough to break into Sofascore's combined XI based on their performances throughout the 2026-27 season so far?

Manchester United's new head coach Mauricio Pochettino will face his first test against Liverpool on Sunday.

United currently sit at 18th in the Premier League after a disappointing start to the season.

Goalkeeper – Alisson Becker (Liverpool).

Between the sticks is Liverpool’s No 1, who since signing for a record fee in 2018, has established himself as one of the best shot-stoppers in the world.

Rated for his positioning, distribution and consistency, Alisson has an impressive record, especially in one-on-one situations.

Sources indicate that the 34-year-old Brazilian goalkeeper has kept four clean sheets in 10 league appearances this season, averaging 2.5 saves per game. He has conceded 10 goals, including a brutal 3-0 loss to Manchester City at Anfield last month.

Alisson was poor in Liverpool's 3-2 defeat by Fenerbahce but responded with a fine display in the Reds' 3-1 win over Crystal Palace when back in league action days later.

Right back – Ronald Araujo (Liverpool).

At right back is Liverpool’s Ronald Araujo, on loan from Barcelona this season, and there are already cries from Liverpool fans to sign him permanently.

The 27-year-old is a natural centre back, but he has done wonders to ease Liverpool’s problems in the right-back position. Jeremie Frimpong started the season in that position but the Liverpool backline were far too exposed. Araujo has helped Liverpool tighten up defensively.

It has been revealed that the Uruguayan defender has featured in all of Liverpool’s league matches so far this season, with his defensive actions helping him contribute inside his own penalty box. He has averaged six clearances per game and has won 30 aerial duels so far this season, behind only Virgil van Dijk in the Liverpool squad.

Ronald Araujo (right) has impressed this season for Liverpool, on loan from Barcelona.

Centre back - Jeremy Jacquet (Liverpool).

Jeremy Jacquet is a young player to watch this season after joining Liverpool this summer.

According to recent reports, the 21-year-old has a 95 per cent accurate pass rate, including long balls. He had a standout performance against Fulham early on in the season, winning five aerial duels, five recoveries and making a clearance off the line to keep his team in the game.

Despite playing in France's second division just two seasons ago, Jacquet has fitted seamlessly into Iraola's style of play at Liverpool and there are suggestions he is an upgrade on the man he replaced, fellow France international Ibrahima Konate.

Centre back - Virgil van Dijk (Liverpool).

It is no surprise that Liverpool and Netherlands team captain Virgil van Dijk makes it into the XI.

Known for his strength, leadership, speed and aerial ability, he is the only defender to win the UEFA Men's Player of the Year Award, and finished runner-up for both the Ballon d'Or and Best FIFA Men's Player in 2019.

This season, he has shown his aerial ability with 3.8 duels won in the air (79 per cent) per game and 4.8 total duels won per game.

The team struggled against Manchester City, however. In the game at Anfield that ended their unbeaten run, Van Dijk only made four defensive contributions and picked up a yellow card for a frustrated foul on Rayan Cherki in added time.

Van Dijk's contract expires next summer, and the 35-year-old has a significant decision to make.

Left back – Kostas Tsimikas (Liverpool).

Is Iraola missing a hidden gem? Tsimikas is very much understudy to Milos Kerkez after acting as a reliable deputy to Andy Robertson.

According to recent reports, but across all competitions this season he is statistically rated higher than the man who's ahead of him in the pecking order. Kerkez is rated at 6.67 – so it is tight.

Nicknamed 'Greek Scouser' by Reds fans, Tsimikas has only started five games but has produced three assists with 1.78 key passes and 1.56 accurate crosses.

Sources indicate that manchester United, on the other hand, have struggled to fill this position. They were unable to recruit in the summer, and now rely on Luke Shaw – who has been sidelined with a muscular problem since limping off during their 1-1 draw with Tottenham Hotspur in October – and are adapting with makeshift alternatives.

Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk celebrates with the fans after beating Crystal Palace.

Centre midfield – Dominik Szoboszlai (Liverpool).

Versatile vice-captain Dominik Szoboszlai signed a newly introduced five-year contract with Liverpool this summer, and has proven his worth after scoring a stoppage-time penalty to level the score in their first game of the season against Newcastle.

With his ability to go forward and send crosses into the box and drop back to defend, Szoboszlai has been crucial for ball recovery, key passes and creating massive chances.

It is a testament to his creative ability, including registering four significant chances and one assist in the Premier League this season, that he makes the XI despite being sidelined with a hamstring injury for three games.

However, the Hungary midfielder has received backlash from fans for playing 90 minutes for his country in a 2-0 win against Georgia in the UEFA Nations League despite early withdrawal against Palace, and injury concerns remain ahead of this afternoon's clash.

Centre midfield – Kobbie Mainoo (Manchester United).

Only one of two Manchester United players in this line-up, Kobbie Mainoo deserves recognition for his creative efforts this season, which have earned him the second highest Sofascore rating in this XI.

In a recent development, the 21-year-old England midfielder is known for his high pressing and long balls to create chances up the pitch. He has also registered four shots from outside the box.

He has been through some turbulent times at Old Trafford but Michael Carrick turned to him regularly this season.

In a recent development, A product of Manchester United's youth system and there is plenty of potential, especially with upcoming manager Mauricio Pochettino’s penchant for developing young players. A chance to refresh and discover his best form.

Kobbie Mainoo is one of only two United players to make the combined XI this weekend.

Centre midfield – Alexis Mac Allister (Liverpool).

After his public revelation that he nearly left Liverpool, Alexis Mac Allister has been in form and pulling the strings in midfield and played an notable role in Liverpool's season so far.

He headed in Liverpool’s second goal in their 3-1 away win over Crystal Palace and his passing and playmaking abilities have been key for their attacking chances this season.

He has scored five goals in 16 appearances across all competitions this season.

Right forward – Bruno Fernandes (Manchester United).

The Portugal forward was named the PFA Players' Player of the Year last season, but he has divided United fans this season.

Inconsistent performances and publicly questioning Carrick's tactics after defeat in Como.

In the 1-1 draw against Spurs at Old Trafford, the skipper did not record his first successful pass until the 23rd minute, and he missed a major chance against Chelsea.

He has bagged four goals and two assists in the Premier League so far, but this is largely owing to his hat-trick against Ipswich, which earned him a perfect 10 Sofascore rating.

United fans will hope he can get back to his old ways under Pochettino.

United fans will be desperate to see Bruno Fernandes find consistent performances again.

Centre-forward – Alexander Isak (Liverpool).

Liverpool’s star striker, transferred for a British record-breaking fee of £125million last summer, has scored eight goals in 14 games this season, showing just how clinical he can be.

Reds fans are finally seeing the form that earned him the significant-money move from Newcastle.

It has been revealed that isak edges out United's Bryan Mbeumo to lead the line in this team. He has a 55.6 per cent big chance conversion, scoring a goal every 113 minutes.

Left forward – Cody Gakpo (Liverpool).

It has been revealed that the Dutchman is establishing himself as Liverpool's go-to wideman among Iraola's plethora of options. His rapid pace and direct approach proves a massive threat.

This season his end product has improved, notching three goals and supplying six assists in 12 appearances across all competitions.

He is proving to be a reliable outlet while summer signings Bradley Barcola and Victor Munoz continue to settle into life in England.

His stunning long-range strike to equalise against Newcastle United highlights just how clinical he can be in front of goal.

He averages 1.9 key passes and one significant chance per game, which lands him a spot in this XI.

Sofascore's combined XI for United's huge trip to Liverpool this afternoon.

Recent findings suggest that davide Possanzini, tecnico del Sudtirol, ha parlato in conferenza stampa al termine della partita persa per 4-1 al "Barbera" contro il Palermo. Queste le sue parole, riprese da StadioNews.it: "L'inizio del Palermo non mi ha sorpreso perché la squadra veniva da una sconfitta e c'era lo stadio pieno. Dovevamo far passare l'ondata, ma è un peccato perché i miei ragazzi stanno lavorando bene: se vogliamo fare un salto di qualità, dobbiamo mettere più convinzione indipendentemente dal risultato. Se un calciatore è bravo, lo faccio giocare anche se è nato nel 2020. Non è la prestazione in sé che mi farà pensare stasera, ma il fatto di dover essere più convinti. Senza nulla togliere al Palermo che è una squadra fortissima e oggi lo ha dimostrato, non ricordo occasioni oltre ai gol".

In a recent development, "Ci è mancata un po' di convinzione - ha ripetuto Possanzini -. Abbiamo fatto cose discrete, subendo il terzo gol quando non dovevamo: iniziare il secondo tempo sul 2-0 sarebbe stato diverso. Le partite vanno giocate prima di perderle, ma noi abbiamo cominciato a giocare quando ormai non c'era più niente da perdere".

Inter, che squadra è lo Stoccarda? Ecco chi tenere d'occhio. E su Jeltsch...

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (351 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Fcinter1908

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that dopo la trasferta contro l'Atalanta, l'Inter ritrova San Siro.
  • "I ragazzi di Hoeness, figlio di Dieter e nipote di Uli, in Champions hanno collezionato sette punti.
  • "Ermedin Demirovic è la punta dello Stoccarda.

Industry observers note that dopo la trasferta contro l'Atalanta, l'Inter ritrova San Siro. I nerazzurri domani scenderanno in campo dove affronteranno lo Stoccarda nella gara valida per la quinta giornata della Fase Campionato della UEFA Champions League. La Gazzetta dello Sport analizza la squadra tedesca, in particolare i punti di forza.

"I ragazzi di Hoeness, figlio di Dieter e nipote di Uli, in Champions hanno collezionato sette punti. In campionato sono a 13. Nell'ultimo turno hanno pareggiato 0-0 con lo Schalke 04. Squadra ostica, difficile da leggere, capace di segnare 27 gol in 16 partite. Football Meets Data aveva sentenziato il "miglior calendario di tutta la Champions" a inizio competizione. Fin qui hanno battuto Viking e Slovan Bratislava, pareggiato 1-1 con l'Atletico e perso con il Galatasaray".

"Ermedin Demirovic è la punta dello Stoccarda. Quest'anno ha segnato 9 gol in 16 partite, di cui quattro nella grande coppa in altrettante gare. Dal 2024 a oggi ha segnato 41 gol in 103 partite con lo Stoccarda. Nel 2025 ha vinto la Coppa di Germania. La storia di Deniz Undav è il manifesto del sacrificio. A 17 anni fu scartato dal Werder Brema perché era "troppo basso" - parole di un vecchio scout -, così inizia a lavorare in fabbrica per duecento euro al mese. Prima di emergere al St. Gilloise, in Belgio, s'è fatto largo nelle serie minori tedesche. Grazie ai gol con lo Stoccarda - 59 in 4 anni - è arrivato anche in nazionale. Media invidiabile: 9 reti in 13 partite".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, il Napoli esce a testa alta dall'Etihad Stadium, sfiorando un'impresa che alla vigilia sembrava quasi impossibile.
  • Il Manchester City prende subito in mano il pallino del gioco e dopo appena due minuti impegna Milinkovic-Savic con una conclusione dalla distanza di Anderson.
  • La partita si accende nella ripresa.

According to recent reports, il Napoli esce a testa alta dall'Etihad Stadium, sfiorando un'impresa che alla vigilia sembrava quasi impossibile. Finisce 2-2 contro il Manchester City, al termine di una splendida prova collettiva della formazione di Massimiliano Allegri, capace di portarsi in vantaggio per ben due volte e di mettere in seria difficoltà gli uomini di Enzo Maresca. Gli azzurri salgono così a quattro punti dopo cinque giornate di Champions League, mentre gli inglesi raggiungono quota dieci. Un pareggio che muove la classifica, ma al di là del peso specifico del punto conquistato è soprattutto la prestazione a rappresentare un'iniezione di fiducia per il Napoli, protagonista di una delle sue migliori serate stagionali.

Il Manchester City prende subito in mano il pallino del gioco e dopo appena due minuti impegna Milinkovic-Savic con una conclusione dalla distanza di Anderson. Il Napoli risponde con due occasioni ravvicinate per McTominay, mentre al 10' O'Reilly non inquadra lo specchio della porta di testa. Gli inglesi fanno possesso, ma sbattono contro una retroguardia azzurra particolarmente attenta, con Olivera e Beukema protagonisti di diverse chiusure provvidenziali. La squadra di Allegri non rinuncia ad attaccare e cresce nel finale di frazione: al 44' proprio Beukema sfiora il vantaggio con un'incornata sugli sviluppi di un calcio d'angolo, trovando la grande risposta di Donnarumma. Si va così all'intervallo sullo 0-0.

La partita si accende nella ripresa. Al 56' Hojlund raccoglie un'imbucata di Gilmour, elude l'intervento di Guehi e trafigge Donnarumma con un diagonale chirurgico. Maresca trova in Doku l'uomo capace di cambiare il volto della sua squadra: il belga semina il panico sulla sinistra e al 67' serve a Bouaddi il pallone dell'1-1. Il City intensifica la pressione, ma proprio nel momento più complicato il Napoli torna avanti: Politano innesca Spinazzola sulla destra, cross dal fondo e splendido destro al volo di Noa Lang al 77'. Gli inglesi si riversano nuovamente in avanti, Gvardiol colpisce un legno e Milinkovic-Savic si oppone ad Anderson. All'86', però, arriva la prodezza di Cherki, che si destreggia tra gli avversari e sorprende il portiere serbo da posizione defilatissima. È il gol del definitivo 2-2, che non cancella la grande prestazione degli azzurri.

Breaking: Kane’s record-equalling cap was no different to his first

⏱️ ~28 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The 125th cap was no different to the first for Harry Kane, who has now been in the business of goal accumulation for so long that it is only at the landmark moments, that all of us are obliged to step back and take in the full scale of the work he has created.
  • Peter Shilton took 20 years to rack up his 125 caps, while for Kane it has been just 11 – and then there are the goals.
  • ✨ Anderson, Rogers and Kane combine beautifully to double England's lead 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 Cap No.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The 125th cap was no different to the first for Harry Kane, who has now been in the business of goal accumulation for so long that it is only at the landmark moments, that all of us are obliged to step back and take in the full scale of the work he has created.

Peter Shilton took 20 years to rack up his 125 caps, while for Kane it has been just 11 – and then there are the goals. Two more on Tuesday took him to 91 which means that only 12 other England players in history have more England caps than Kane has England goals. This unassuming man from Chingford, who looks like a mildly rebellious academic from the late 1950s, was at it again: the first-time strike, the back-post header. He has some misses across these 11 years, most infamously from the penalty spot against France at the Qatar World Cup almost four years ago, so, yes, there are some regrets too. But what sticks is the way he has taken his chances – again and again.

ONE-TOUCH BRILLIANCE! ✨ Anderson, Rogers and Kane combine beautifully to double England's lead 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 Cap No. 125, goal No. 90 for the skipper 👏 https://t.co/otMcxlXyps.

Following his debut goal in 2015 against Lithuania, Kane has missed just 27 of the 152 England games since. He has added to the total like a great Test batsman patiently moving the scoreboard along. There was a bad run without goals in 2020 and before that in 2018. He scored only five in his first 17 caps and then scored 14 in his next 10. Against a very mediocre Czech Republic team this was classic late-era Kane, picking his moments and taking those chances with the usual absence of nerves. He was even substituted before the end.

Hall ➡️ Kane! The Newcastle fullback swings in the corner and it's the England captain who rises highest to head home 💥 https://t.co/5EhAcNZUqm.

Recent findings suggest that afterwards at a Wembley press conference to mark the occasion, he invoked the cricket analogy himself on the question of scoring 100 England goals. “Being in the 90s, I try not to think about it too much, and it’s like I guess being a cricketer in the 90s. The more you think about the hundred… you don’t always get there.” There has still not been the elusive major trophy in the Kane England years but there has been success relative to the three decades that came before it. Semi-finals, finals – a good team if not a winning team.

At the centre of it has been a man around whom there has never been any scandal or, by the usual measure, much that might be described as spectacular. Rather it has been the scope of Kane’s career that is the most striking. The volume of the goals, of appearances, the capacity to be available – to play, to score – and the absolute quality of the player himself. He is determined to wring the very last drop out of his talent and usually refuses to acknowledge the prospect of the end, although there was a nod to it this time. “At some stage you know this opportunity isn’t going to be here,” he mentioned. “I’m not going to be around forever, and I still hope that’s a long way away. But ultimately, of course, there’s times you’re tired or you’re injured, but I know I’ll miss it when it’s done. I try to always remind myself that and always try to make myself available.”.

It has been revealed that one expects that when the end comes it will not be as rancorous as the final exit of Cristiano Ronaldo from Portugal, a drama playing out elsewhere. At some point, Kane will take his leave and it is likely to be as unassuming as the rest of it. He will be back at Wembley, injury permitting, for cap No 126 next month against Croatia. He talks like a different person to the one he was even five years ago – with a confidence and certainty about his place in the world. As opposed to the younger Kane, who seemed to regard everything outside his goalscoring tunnel vision with a general sense of bemusement.

“Availability,” he said, “is one of the biggest strengths you can have at this level for any coach.” He was keen to emphasise his “all-round leadership” too, “a lot of assets off the pitch”. He still measures himself in goals, of course, and perhaps there will be a Ballon d’Or too later this month – a prize that has eluded generations of England players before him who have won much more for their clubs than Kane has done. The good news for Kane is that his last England years will be spent in a very good England team – one which was on another level to its opposition on this occasion too.

Recent findings suggest that no team in the top tier of the Nations League has scored more goals than England – 14 in the last four match days. Tuchel’s name was sung at Wembley and even if the World Cup semi-final collapse in Atlanta in July has not been entirely forgotten, the roughest edges have been taken off somewhat. Another great performance from Jude Bellingham and also from Morgan Rogers, in place of Bukayo Saka. Another dominant Elliot Anderson performance in midfield. They left Wembley to applause and a sense of optimism renewed.

Recent findings suggest that england kept the ball with such authority, and none more so than Bellingham. Trent Alexander-Arnold came back at right-back. Myles Lewis-Skelly returned for another bite at a Wembley midfield job. As in Prague last week, there was a self-inflicted Czech calamity in the first half. The captain Vladimir Coufal appeared to lose his cool at the threat of the England attack all over the Czechs’ half. No other reason for this Premier League experienced full-back to fling himself at Kane’s cross and drill the ball past Newcastle goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek on 27 minutes.

In a recent development, england lead! 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿⚽️ A great ball from Kane and a great finish from Coufal - unfortunately for the defender, it's in the wrong net...🫣 https://t.co/h54xQnunZM.

The second goal, on 40 minutes, was one for the ages. Anderson’s ball out to the right was met first time by Rogers for the cross and Kane ran into the space, as he has done so many times, to deliver a finish struck with customary assuredness. Bellingham almost flicked in Rogers’s cross on 56 minutes and from the corner that came after, Kane nodded in a header at the back post from Lewis Hall’s cross. All remarked, the defending was woeful but there was nothing wrong with the finish.

Thomas Tuchel believes England have taken a step forward from their World Cup heartbreak over this international break and noted he was “honoured” to hear fans sing his name.

England finished their four Nations League games with a 3-0 win over Czech Republic, in which Harry Kane scored twice on his record-equalling 125th appearance.

It meant that Tuchel’s team have won three and lost one, against Spain, of their four games since the World Cup, after which the England head coach was heavily criticised for the semi-final defeat to Argentina.

Tuchel seems to have won the forgiveness of some England supporters, who sang his name at the start and the end of Tuesday’s game.

“It means a lot,” Tuchel said. “It’s amazing to have a song. It’s the biggest honour. And I’m very happy and very honoured. They can be sure that I will give my absolute best to make our team win and play well.”.

Asked if he sensed a change in mood around his England team since the fall-out from the World Cup, Tuchel said: “I do and I think it’s necessary to move on. I think I can only repeat that we didn’t go out in the group stage. Sometimes it feels like that and we didn’t. As I said, our aim was always to progress, move forward and improve.”.

Tuchel snapped back at a reporter who questioned why he felt it necessary to repeat that England had not gone out in the group stage of the World Cup, claiming the criticism had felt a “little bit” too harsh.

According to recent reports, but on whether England have shown they are a step ahead of where the team were at the World Cup during this international camp, Tuchel was far more positive and replied: “Of course and that’s what we have to do. That is our goal to constantly improve and develop.

“We had these experiences together and we had a major tournament together, and it was very positive. It’s necessary to move forward and improve, especially in sports. This is what we’re trying to do.

Recent findings suggest that “We adjusted some details in our structure and we didn’t compromise on the effort and the intensity, and on the togetherness of the team. The players who were with us in the World Cup took care of these standards and of the culture within the team, off the pitch and on the pitch, and I think that’s what you could see.”.

It has been revealed that we played a very good match, very fluid and to put it into context it was the fourth match in 11 or 12 days. We dominated the whole match, had some good opportunities, scored some beautiful goals. Subs were strong. Very good performance again.

[Leading the way, Mr Kane] Of course. That’s what he does. I don’t take it for granted. It’s just exceptional, every single match. It’s just difficult to find new words to express it.

Training, attitude, cohesion, belief, of course [is why they’re stronger than ever].

It has been revealed that [Has the World Cup made England stronger?]  Of course, we got the first medal in 60 years. We didn’t go out in the group stage. We had a strong qualification, strong World Cup and strong camp. All four matches were on a high level. The camp throughout from the first day was on the highest level. You learn every day together. We grew stronger.

It has been revealed that I was happy that everyone who was in the camp was contributing. Everyone was on the pitch. Everyone demonstrated he was willing to give everything for the team and for the shirt. The guys who were with us for the World Cup set the standards high, made everyone feel welcome and everyone had a good camp.

According to recent reports, he’s the best England player evert to wear the shirt and it’s an honour to play with him. And he’s only getting better.

Recent findings suggest that A perfect night for me personally and also for the team. It’s been a tough camp, a long camp with some difficult games so it’s nice to finish it off all together. An extremely proud evening for me.

According to recent reports, you saw some fantastic football out there tonight. The way we’re moving, the one-touch stuff, a fantastic ball from Elliot to Morgan and then a first time cross which was as good as it gets. As a striker you’re just waiting for those opportunities.

In a recent development, it started in the first game [reaching a higher level] although the result didn’t go for us. First game after a tournament, obviously this was a four-game camp, we had to find it [a higher level] and find it swiftly. That’s the most pleasing thing.

This is the England team. There’s always going to be competition for places. It’s about taking the opportunity whether it’s 90 minutes, five minutes, whatever it was, make the most of it. You’re seeing that, everyone wants to be part of this. That’s only going to make us better for sure.

[Now for cap 126 next month?] That would be nice for sure.

Because places between teams who finish on the same points in the first instance are decided on head-to-heads, Croatia will have to beat England 8-0 at Wembley next month to have any hope of stopping them from qualifying for the quarter-finals.

First win at Wembley in four, three wins in succession, 14 goals in four games and three clean sheets in a row.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • We do not know why Cole Palmer headed for the tunnel in a huff after full-time while others in the same Chelsea side paraded the pitch to thank those supporters who had stayed to the end.
  • Sources indicate that perhaps he was frustrated with himself after a performance in which he did not score, assist, or even test James Trafford in Leeds United’s goal.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By KIERAN GILL, MAIL SPORT REPORTER.

Published: 01:47 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 04:11 EST, 22 November 2026.

We do not know why Cole Palmer headed for the tunnel in a huff after full-time while others in the same Chelsea side paraded the pitch to thank those supporters who had stayed to the end.

Sources indicate that perhaps he was frustrated with himself after a performance in which he did not score, assist, or even test James Trafford in Leeds United’s goal. Maybe he did not fancy thanking those who had been booing as Chelsea trailed 4-1. It is possible he simply does not like losing.

Most superstars can feel the same, and they can show their stroppy side when the game is not going their way.

Industry observers note that an extreme example is Bruno Fernandes. Manchester United fans have long accepted his reputation as the Premier League’s temperamental nonpareil because of the numbers he can produce with the whingeing, albeit not so much this season during their downturn.

Such names can get away with petulance when their performances are proper, though Palmer has no such justification right now. The 24-year-old Englishman, unfortunately for Chelsea, put up another anonymous 90 minutes.

Sources indicate that we could see he was frustrated even while on the pitch towards the end, with the way he was performatively kicking passes backwards as if to tell everyone else he had no other option. We have seen that before when Chelsea are losing, and it can be somewhat unhelpful when the pressure is being piled on the manager. It indicates the tactical set-up is not to his liking.

Industry observers note that cole Palmer and Joao Pedro were involved in a frosty exchange following Chelsea's 4-1 home defeat by Leeds. Source: Instagram/farihaxchels.

As the biggest name within this Chelsea team and a player whose profile transcends his team-mates’, like it or not, he is the totem when it is all going wrong.

In a recent development, we wax lyrical when he is at his brilliant best. It can be as if there has been an explosion at a praise factory when he is dropping that shoulder to down a helpless defender. We know how terrifically talented he is. He is still compared to that 2023-24 season when his statistics were, in a wonderful way, stupid.

But when he is not performing, so too does he need to take the medicine of disapproval, which came in the form of a chorus of boos aimed at all those in Chelsea shirts at Stamford Bridge.

Industry observers note that leeds had not won at this ground since 1999. They corrected history, then Complaining Cole showed up at full-time.

His reaction did not speak to the cultural reset which Chelsea hoped they had orchestrated in the summer when they finally signed some experience for the changing room, bringing in Danny Welbeck, the 35-year-old whom Palmer has nominated as their newly introduced ‘Unc’ after Tosin Adarabioyo’s departure, and Jordan Henderson, 36.

It was a poor show from someone who, in his fourth season at a club that gave him his chance when spending £42.5million to sign him from Manchester City in 2023, should be seen as a leader by now.

Palmer is, probably, still undroppable. Alonso would create an almighty problem for himself if he suddenly relegated his No10 to the substitutes’ bench when playing Nottingham Forest next week. But he is in danger of such conversations cropping up at a time when he should want to be impressing enough to get back into Thomas Tuchel’s England squad at the next opportunity.

We are told both Palmer and Levi Colwill are desperate to represent their country again, but neither are performing to that standard of late. Colwill is a defender devoid of confidence, questioning himself and making mistakes. There was one moment during this demoralising defeat by Leeds when he booted a long ball straight out of play and reprimanded himself for it.

Sources indicate that colwill is perfectly capable of playing a good game. You do not have multiple clubs including Bayern Munich making enquiries with Chelsea without being considered elite. He is in a bad spell, and can come back from it, just like Palmer.

Inevitably, the response of some on social media was to say that Alonso’s time should be up.

For clarity, he is not under threat of suddenly being sacked by those at the top of Chelsea. He is 11 Premier League games into his career, and, clearly, deserves time.

The tactics are on him, absolutely. But he is also dealing with a few issues outside of his control, such as holes in his squad and injuries inflicted, like his highly-influential vice captain Moises Caicedo having to be substituted after 22 minutes in this match.

Xabi Alonso has made errors but was rightly considered a huge coup when Chelsea landed him.

When appointed head coach of Bayer Leverkusen in October 2022, they went through patches in the Bundesliga. First, they beat Schalke 4-0, which was good. Then they failed to win any of their next three fixtures, which was bad.

Then they won five in a row – happy days. Then they won only one of their following five – bad days. Then they won five in a row again – perfect. Then they won only one of their next seven – pitiful.

But the following season, Leverkusen won the Bundesliga without losing a single game. Alonso was considered an almighty coup when secured in the summer. A little patience is deserved from my perspective, even if Chelsea are currently in a dismal spell.

It is hard not to think Malo Gusto’s time at Chelsea is almost at an end.

He was priced out of a move in the summer when the club asked for £75million, with Liverpool, Manchester City and others across Europe indicating their interest in that window.

Malo Gusto cut a lonely figure after being beaten for Leeds's fourth goal.

But the 23-year-old Frenchman has shown little worth as the season has progressed.

Gusto started in five of Alonso’s first six games in all competitions at the beginning of the campaign.

Industry observers note that since then, he has been handed one start in eight, and that was in the Carabao Cup at Liverpool. Coming on as a substitute in this loss to Leeds, he tried and failed to play Brenden Aaronson offside and was then beaten by his man as the visitors made it 4-1.

We should expect to hear more on Gusto’s situation as January approaches.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Middlesbrough are flying high in the Championship, with Saturday’s victory over Bristol City moving them top of the table. Ahead of Tuesday’s clash with Swansea City though, potential January transfer window reinforcements were on Kim Hellberg’s mind.

And, the Boro boss said that the midfield is an area that needs to be bolstered. His statement comes after a long-term hamstring injury to Rokas Pukstas, while Connor Barron is out of favour and also dealing with an injury problem of his own.

Speaking to The Northern Echo, Hellberg said: “So, if you look at all those things, of course we need to strengthen that in January, absolutely.”.

Hellberg is right in saying that a upcoming midfielder is an absolute must for Middlesbrough. The injury to Pukstas and Barron’s absence and lack of favour mean that the Boro boss’ options in the middle of the park have dwindled significantly.

Industry observers note that however, whoever joins has a tough battle on their hands to get into the team. American teammates Aidan Morris and Sebastian Berhalter have forged an excellent partnership in the first third of the campaign, and they are going to prove tough to dislodge.

Riley McGree can drop into a deeper role if needs be, but he is at his best in a more attacking role. The same goes for Myles Peart-Harris, so a defence-minded midfielder would bring more balance and depth to the department.

The player signed will have to be up for the fight to break into the team though. They may also have to accept that starting opportunities could be somewhat limited, with Morris and Berhalter among the Championship’s best performers of the season to date.

Sources indicate that middlesbrough spent big in the summer, with much of the funds going towards reinforcements in attack and defence. Will Lankshear and Ashley Phillips joined from Spurs for sizeable fees, and a package deal worth £14m was struck for Radek Vitek.

In a recent development, berhalter, Peart-Harris and Pukstas joined as latest midfielders. But of those, Boro’s new American star Berhalter cost less than £900,000 up front, and Peart-Harris was signed on a free transfer.

Industry observers note that despite the busy summer transfer window, it is clear that a latest midfielder is needed. Boro can not afford to rest on their laurels in the Championship promotion push, with a deep and talented squad needed to deal with the rigours of a 46-game league season.

At least one midfielder – preferably a defence-first one – could help push Hellberg and co over the line after last season’s Championship play-off heartbreak.

It has been revealed that È stata dura, il Como passa per 1-0 sull'AEK Atene grazie a una perla sensazionale di Luis Milla al 57': non c'è ancora aritmetica certezza per i lariani di Fabregas, ma con 12 punti è quasi fatta ormai per i playoff. Finisce ancora al tappeto, per la quarta partita di fila, la formazione ellenica in Europa.

Primo tempo contratto ma acceso a tratti al Sinigaglia, dove i tifosi dell'AEK Atene hanno scaldato l'ambiente fin dall'annuncio delle formazioni. Dopo il tiro potente ma impreciso di Kutesa, lasciato libero di avanzare sulla spizzata di Jovic, il Como ha costruito l'occasione più nitida all'8', con Nico Paz che ha lanciato in profondità Tasos Douvikas, ma la manovra dei lariani è rimasta prevedibile e poco incisiva. Il momento chiave è arrivato al 28': Alex Valle è stato steso da Majer in area, ma dal dischetto il capitano Lucas Da Cunha, fino a quel momento rigorista infallibile, ha mandato la palla a lato, sprecando l'1-0. Nel finale di frazione è stato l'AEK a rendersi pericoloso, con la doppia chance Gacinovic-Rota che ha impegnato i riflessi di Robert Sanchez, e si è andati al riposo sullo 0-0.

Rientrati in campo i nervi sono rimasti piuttosto tesi, per una ripresa contratta e priva di luce in avanti da inseguire per andare in gol da parte del Como. L’AEK Atene galvanizzato dal primo tempo senza subire reti e Vitalis a ricevere in area e girarsi bene ma sparare altissimo in ottima zona. Con gli spazi intasati dai giganti Relvas-Moukoudi e una compattezza tra i reparti rilevante, è servita l’illuminazione improvvisa di Luis Milla per stappare una partita così scorbutica e sporca. Al 57’, ricevendo da Baturina largo a sinistra, il regista spagnolo si è spostato palla per disegnare una traiettoria da sognano sul secondo palo per l’1-0 vincente. Una stoccata imprendibile per Strakosha che ha facilitato la vita alla banda di Cesc Fabregas lungo il match, spendendosi tra duelli e scintille in campo.

Scattata l’ora di gioco Jacobo Ramon su palla scodellata da Milla ha sfiorato per centimetri il secondo palo dell’ex portiere della Lazio per il possibile raddoppio, rischiando all’81’. Una scivolata in piena area su Varga a tu per tu con Robert Sanchez lasciava presagire guai, ma l’arbitro Alberola Rojas su silent check del VAR Cuadra Fernandez non è cascato nell’inganno del giocatore dell’AEK che avrebbe voluto strappare il rigore del pari. Tra sostituzioni e cartellini gialli estratti dal direttore di gara spagnolo, una galoppata targata Perrone per poco stava per sorprendere la formazione ellenica per il 2-0, ma non ha angolato a sufficienza. Nemmeno Nico Paz allo scadere con un colpo di testa alto sopra la traversa, completamente smarcato. Poco male perché il triplice fischio il Como ha ottenuto il bottino pieno: 3 punti per portarsi a quota 12 e al terzo posto momentaneo in Champions League. L'aritmetica certezza non c'è ancora ma i biancoblù sono vicinissimi al pass per i playoff ormai. La formazione di Nikolic cade ancora fuori casa in Europa e resta a mani vuote.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Antonio Nocerino, allenatore del Napoli Primavera, ha parlato dopo la sconfitta contro il Manchester City per 4-1 in Youth League:.

Recent findings suggest that “Siamo partiti male. Sembra che quando giochiamo queste partite si pensi di più a quello che c’è intorno, al rispetto per l’altra squadra, e non si pensi più a ciò che si deve fare in campo. Ai ragazzi per il secondo tempo ho detto di mettere ciò che avevano, di giocare, perché non avevano nulla da perdere, con coraggio e intensità. Abbiamo avuto delle opportunità, abbiamo preso una traversa, poi ci sono state delle situazioni a nostro favore che potevano essere finalizzate in maniera diversa. Mi porto a casa la reazione, l’approccio della ripresa, ovviamente sapendo anche contro chi abbiamo giocato. Va dato anche merito all’avversario, sono forti.

In a recent development, club Brugge? Noi in tutte le partite vogliamo provare a fare risultato, anche lì, se dobbiamo chiudere, dobbiamo farlo nel migliore dei modi. Dev’esserci sempre quella speranza che non deve mai mancare. Dobbiamo giocarcela come sempre, l’obiettivo è fare bene e portare soprattutto in casa a vincere. È un sogno però ci vogliamo provare fino alla fine.

Recent findings suggest that campionato e Coppa Italia? Dobbiamo lavorare bene e recuperare le forze, oltre a mettere una mentalità un po’ diversa. Dobbiamo cercare di essere più aggressivi, vogliosi, più forti nell’uno contro uno e finalizzare un po’ di più quello che creiamo. Costruiamo tanto, arriviamo negli ultimi metri, ma abbiamo poca cattiveria nel chiudere l’azione. È una situazione secondo me individuale e mentale di ogni singolo giocatore. Noi alleniamo tanto i tiri e le situazioni di gioco, però poi c’è anche l’individualità del giocatore. Quando noi ti mettiamo in una condizione di tirare o di fare l’azione da gol, bisogna avere la cattiveria, la fame di fare gol. A noi manca un po’ questo. Finora siamo stati un po’ troppo ‘belli’, e in alcune situazioni dobbiamo essere un po’ più sporchi”.

Scegli Fcinter1908.it come tuo sito preferito su Google: clicca qui.

Intervistato da La Gazzetta dello Sport, il doppio ex di Inter e Stoccarda Hansi Muller ha parlato della sfida di domani sera a San Siro:.

«Non vedo l’ora di tornare a Milano, a San Siro, anche per tirare fuori poi il mio dialetto milanese. L’Italia mi ha migliorato come persona, mi ha arricchito con amicizie profonde, sempre attive».

Recent findings suggest that lei è stato il primo nei quattro trasferimenti diretti tra Stoccarda e Inter. Poi sono arrivati Klinsmann, Sammer e Kuzmanovic. Come è stato scoperto?

It has been revealed that «Dovevo venire già dopo che abbiamo vinto gli Europei nell’80. Avevo 23 anni, pensavo che fosse troppo presto. Sandro Mazzola e il ds Giancarlo Beltrami vennero a Monaco per una partita della Germania contro l’Austria: abbiamo vinto 1-0, avevo segnato e il gol è stato anche eletto il migliore del mese. Ho spiegato la mia idea e loro virarono su Herbert Prohaska».

Sources indicate that «No, e due anni dopo, l’austriaco è andato alla Roma: loro si sono ripresentati. Beltrami mi ha portato un modellino di San Siro in miniatura, con una base di marmo, lo stadio bellissimo, con lo stemma dell’Inter. L’ha tirato fuori da una tasca, non era più grande come un cellulare. Mi disse: “In questo stadio tu puoi giocare”. Non ho mai dimenticato quel momento. E quella riproduzione del Meazza l’ho donata al museo del calcio tedesco di Dortmund. Resterà sempre lì, come ricordo».

Cosa significava l’Inter a quei tempi?

«Tre aspetti: primo, aveva sempre un grande nome. Juve, Milan e Inter erano sempre molto attraenti. Secondo è chiaro che potevi guadagnare di più, un argomento che aiuta nel cambiare la società o andare all’estero. Però la terza cosa, vista anche oggi, è per me la più importante: vivere in un altro paese, in un posto eccezionale come l’Italia, imparare la lingua, adattarsi a questo ambiente, alla cultura, a un modo di vivere ti fa crescere. Oggi a 69 anni sono convinto che quello che vale di più è la persona, è l’uomo, e non la coppa che hai in vetrina. Chiaro che vuoi vincere dei titoli quando giochi, ma contano di più le persone. Dopo oltre 40 anni ho ancora amici e contatti frequenti con l’Italia. Nei giorni scorsi mi sono sentito con Fulvio Collovati, quando ho visto Bergomi al funerale di Brehme ci siamo abbracciati come due fratelli. Vuol dire che ho lasciato un buon ricordo».

E la nostra lingua non l’ha mai dimenticata.

It has been revealed that «Già. Ho anche approfittato del fatto che c’erano solo due stranieri, allora dovevi imparare per forza l’italiano. E i primi sei mesi sono stato solo a Milano, mia moglie non poteva licenziarsi dalla Mercedes e mi ha raggiunto solo a Natale. Mi ha sentito parlare al telefono un quarto d’ora con dei vostri colleghi ed era stupita. “Cosa sta succedendo? Ma come parli? Incredibile”».

Sources indicate that veniamo all’Inter di oggi: anche con l’Atalanta si è mostrata una squadra a due facce, come i suoi risultati stagionali. Spiegazioni?

Industry observers note that «Negli ultimi anni è sempre in cima, tra scudetti e finali di Champions. Per gli avversari è sempre una partita molto attraente, importante, mettono qualche “percento” in più per fare bella figura contro l’Inter. Tu quindi devi essere sempre al 100%, ma è difficile presentarsi sempre perfetto. Se ti manca solo il 5% gli altri ne approfittano. L’Inter è un po’ come il Bayern. È la numero uno, e tutti gli altri danno di più, quando la incontrano, è una partita fuori dal normale. Se sei sotto tono rischi, si è visto in questa stagione».

According to recent reports, lo Stoccarda invece che squadra è? Ha un punto in più dell’Inter in Champions.

«Noi diciamo wundertüte , il sacchetto delle sorprese, non sai cosa trovi. Non ha una sola faccia. Però l’Inter non deve sottovalutarla. Se i suoi osservatori hanno visto la prima mezzora con l’Atletico, non succederà. Gli spagnoli avranno pensato, “vabbè è solo lo Stoccarda”, e sono stati dominati all’inizio. Poi è finita 1-1, ma per mezzora i nostri avevano un’occasione ogni due minuti. L’Inter non li prenderà sotto gamba se ha analizzato questa partita. Era una mia piccola speranza, però sono sicuro che non succederà più».

Quali sono le caratteristiche dello Stoccarda?

Recent findings suggest that «Sebastian Hoeness è un bravo allenatore e ha il vantaggio di confrontarsi quasi tutti i giorni con il padre Dieter, ex grande centravanti e manager. Se tu hai come consigliere una leggenda che è anche tuo padre, lui vuole il meglio per te, ti dice le cose come stanno. Tutto lo staff è giovane, quindi più vicino all’età della rosa. Sanno come funzionano alcuni meccanismi mentali dei giocatori. Loro fanno dei capolavori. C’è molto affiatamento, e poi un altro aspetto».

It has been revealed that «È una squadra con molti mancini. Anche quattro o cinque possono essere titolari. E parlo da mancino, noi siamo meno prevedibili, un po’ come nel tennis. Se ce ne sono tanti, possono causare difficoltà agli avversari. Sto parlando di Chabot, Hendriks, Mittelstädt, Stiller, Spalt. Con loro è un altro gioco».

Vi siete accorti anche in Germania di Pio Esposito?

«Sì, ragazzo eccezionale, visto anche in Nazionale, sta facendo grandi cose».

Sources indicate that dopo lo Stoccarda per l’Inter ci sarà il Borussia Dortmund, attuale capolista della Bundesliga. Sarà un ostacolo più duro?

In a recent development, «Il Borussia Dortmund non è migliore dello Stoccarda. Sono primi in Bundesliga, però con noi hanno vinto con molta fortuna, non è al livello del Bayern».

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that west Ham sold the midfielder to the Belgian side in the last transfer window. WHUFC gave their academy graduate the green light to head out the exit door on a permanent basis.

Sources indicate that potts, 23, penned a long-term contract with Club Brugge running until June 2030. He has made 16 appearances in all competitions since his move abroad, four of which have come in the Champions League, and he has chipped in with one assist.

It has been revealed that he has opened up about his exit from the London Stadium on BBC Radio 5 Live’s Euro Leagues Show: “In pre-season my minutes with West Ham were limited, they weren’t as much as I wanted and then I spoke with my agent and said ‘let’s explore options because this season I’m 22, turning 23’. It’s a massive part of my career and I wanted to play. The opportunity of Club Brugge came along with Champions League football, the best club in Belgium and it was an opportunity I couldn’t really turn down with how my minutes were going down with West Ham.

“I grew up in the area, going to the stadium watching the games. It was always going to be a tough decision but it was something that I had to do for my career. It was an emotional decision because it had to be made quite quickly. It’s been the right decision for me and so far I’m enjoying it, I’m loving life here.”.

West Ham are well stocked up with options in Potts’ position. WHUFC have the likes of Arne Engels, Divine Mukasa, Edson Alvarez and Tomas Soucek, among others, at their disposal.

Therefore, Potts wouldn’t have played many minutes for the Hammers this season. His decision to leave for Club Brugge has worked out well for him so far.

Sources indicate that the Barking-born man has become a key player for his current club. He is also getting exposure to European football which will do him good.

Potts rose up through West Ham’s ranks and was a regular for them at various different youth levels as a youngster. He was loaned out to Wycombe Wanderers and Portsmouth in the EFL to get some experience under his belt and to boost his development.

According to recent reports, he made his first-team debut for the Hammers back in 2021 in a Europa League clash against Dinamo Zagreb. He went on to make a further 32 outings for the London outfit, 25 of which came in the last campaign.

Recent findings suggest that potts has settled into life at Club Brugge with relative ease. His side take on Liverpool at home in the Champions League on Wednesday night and they are 2nd in their league table behind Royale Union Saint-Gilloise.

In a recent development, west Ham will be disappointed to have seen him depart but they couldn’t offer him consistent minutes anymore due to too much competition for places. The Hammers have seen their form in the Championship slump over recent weeks.

They have recently turned to Scott Parker as their fresh manager but the ex-Fulham and Burnley man has struggled to make an impact so far. His side drew 1-1 at home against Preston North End last time out and couldn’t find a winner.

Tutte le novità per la Supercoppa Italiana dal 2027 al 2030: si riparte dalla gara secca, ma resta l'opzione estero.

In a recent development, la Lega Calcio Serie A ha ufficialmente approvato e reso pubblico il bando per i diritti audiovisivi della Supercoppa Italiana sul territorio italiano per il triennio 2027/28, 2028/29 e 2029/30, disegnando un quadro che lega strettamente aspetti sportivi e ritorni economici. Il primo cambiamento strutturale è la separazione della Supercoppa dalla Coppa Italia nella vendita dei diritti, una scelta che dà alla competizione un percorso commerciale autonomo per i prossimi tre anni.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Per chi si aggiudicherà i diritti televisivi, la novità principale è la possibilità esclusiva di acquistare anche il pacchetto di title sponsorship legato al torneo. Non è fissato un prezzo minimo di partenza: le emittenti dovranno formulare una propria offerta economica, indicando anche un corrispettivo aggiuntivo in caso di formula a quattro squadre. Chi otterrà questo abbinamento potrà legare il proprio nome alla competizione e al premio per il migliore in campo, oltre a ottenere visibilità a bordocampo, sul trofeo e sulla patch applicata alla manica destra delle maglie delle squadre partecipanti. Sul fronte della trasmissione, le eventuali semifinali potranno andare in onda anche a pagamento, mentre per la finale restano fermi gli obblighi di diffusione in chiaro previsti dalla normativa sugli eventi di particolare rilevanza sociale.

It has been revealed that sul piano del calendario, la Lega cercherà un'intesa con il licenziatario per stabilire il periodo di svolgimento del torneo, ma si riserva comunque l'ultima parola se non si dovesse raggiungere un accordo. Come criterio base il bando riporta la Supercoppa alla formula tradizionale della gara secca tra la vincitrice del campionato e quella della Coppa Italia, fissando un prezzo minimo di 8 milioni di euro a stagione (24 milioni complessivi nel triennio). Resta però aperta la strada della Final Four: la Lega può scegliere a propria discrezione di attivarla in una o più stagioni del bando, con le prime due classificate in campionato e le due finaliste di Coppa Italia (e l'eventuale ripescaggio di terza e quarta in Serie A), incassando in quel caso 7 milioni di euro in più per ciascuna edizione. A pesare sulla decisione tra finale a due o a quattro sarà soprattutto la sede, dato che resta la possibilità di giocare sia in Italia sia all'estero.

  • Bruno Fernandes has revealed there are no ongoing contract negotiations with Manchester United after he rejected their proposed new deal.
  • The Manchester United captain's contract is set to expire in June 2027, which means that if the club and player fail to agree fresh terms, Fernandes will be free to discuss a summer move with clubs abroad as early as the January transfer window.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By KATE MCGREAVY, EXECUTIVE SPORTS EDITOR.

Published: 04:01 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 05:10 EST, 22 November 2026.

Bruno Fernandes has revealed there are no ongoing contract negotiations with Manchester United after he rejected their proposed new deal.

The Manchester United captain's contract is set to expire in June 2027, which means that if the club and player fail to agree fresh terms, Fernandes will be free to discuss a summer move with clubs abroad as early as the January transfer window.

Fernandes has divided United fans during their dire season so far but new manager Mauricio Pochettino confirmed he will remain as captain in his first press conference on Friday.

It was widely known that discussions between Fernandes and Man United began over the summer, on the heels of a strong campaign which saw him named Men's PFA Player of the Year.

But Fernandes has now shed light on his future by admitting contract talks have stalled after the club put a deal on the table.

In a recent development, 'No, there's no negotiations ongoing,' Fernandes told Sky Sports ahead of United's trip to Anfield this afternoon. 'But I've seen people saying that he's asked for more money, he's asked for more years. If I wanted more money I wouldn't be here.

Bruno Fernandes has revealed there are no ongoing contract negotiations with Man United.

Sources indicate that 'I had somewhere to go to get much more money than being at Manchester United. I could have been in a place that is much warmer than Manchester. Two summers ago, three summers ago, last summer, I always had a chance to leave and I always chose to be here.

'The thing is I've always showed how much I care about the club and how much I want to win at this club.

'And I've always mentioned the moment the club thinks is the time for me to move on, I will move on. I'm not going to be the player that I've seen many in this time at Man United they're going to stay here just by staying, just by finishing my contract and then we will see.

'In the moment the club indicates "Bruno, it's time to part ways", I'm going to be the first one walking out the door.

'Yeah the club offered me a newly introduced contract so I think that from their side shows that they want me to stay.

'As I said there are no negotiations going on. We spoke about the contract at the end of last season. We came in the beginning of the season speaking about the contract but about the context of the team and the club I just put that to a side because I don't think it's the right moment, neither for me, neither for the club to be talking about negotiations because the most notable thing now is that the club gets back to winning games.'.

Industry observers note that the club may yet seek to trigger the 12-month extension in Fernandes' contract. Daily Mail Sport understands Galatasaray as well as AC Milan and Saudi are among those monitoring developments.

The Portuguese was linked with a big-money move to Saudi Arabia last year with Al-Hilal reportedly willing to offer a contract worth up to £200m to the midfielder, on top of a £100m transfer fee to United, but he chose to commit his future to the Red Devils.

United currently sit in the relegation zone after a 40-year worst-ever start to the season. Fernandes publicly questioned the former manager's tactics after his side's Champions League thrashing at the hands of Como, and has struggled to find form this season.

Fernandes was brought back into the fold after going through a brief period of being frozen out of Michael Carrick's squad following his incendiary comments following defeat in Italy last month.

Fernandes, who is usually very deliberate in what he says in the media, was scathing in his criticism of coaches after the Como debacle.

'It's a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave a little space in behind and try to get the ball in the first moment, to wait for them, to give them the ball,' he stated.

'But sometimes when you give too much the ball to these teams they get confident, they have so many bodies behind the ball that make you run a lot, make people get frustrated, and then obviously when you recover the ball the legs are, and the brain, much more difficult to make it work.'.

Industry observers note that his post-Como interview was widely condemned by fans and pundits alike, with Gary Neville lamenting: 'If that's your captain saying that, imagine what they're saying in the dressing room behind closed doors when no one's listening. That's horrific.'.

He also told Fernandes to 'read the room' and accused him of being an 'excuse merchant' on his podcast.

Fernandes was left on the bench for Man United's next Premier League appointment, a loss to Bournemouth, before returning to the starting XI against Chelsea the following matchday.

After Man United's comeback win against Roma, Fernandes was defiant in his post-match remarks as he stressed that he had not been sanctioned for undermining Carrick with his initial interview.

Sources indicate that 'The club needed that win. The players needed that win. It is something we needed as a group of players and staff,' he said. 'We have been working so hard to get out of this situation together. It has been tough. There has been a lot of speculation in the media.

Mauricio Pochettino confirmed Fernandes will remain as captain in his first press conference.

'A lot of lies around many things that have happened at this club, between me and the manager, like that we have cleared the air. Nothing like that happened.

'The manager took a decision of making myself on the bench because I wasn't performing. And that's fair.

It has been revealed that 'Everyone felt like that was a punishment for the words that I had [after Como]. And if it was, it was right.

According to recent reports, 'The manager makes the decisions. I have to accept it. I have to go forward with that. It doesn't change the belief I have in the manager, the staff and every player at this club.

'And it doesn't change my aim to win every f***ing game that I have ahead of me.'.

Fernandes' comments were ultimately unable to keep Carrick in his job however, with the former club captain finally sacked on November 11 after an agonising three-day wait.

Man United's hierarchy, notably chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox, have come under fire from the fanbase and within the club for their treatment of the departing coach, with Carrick taking two days of training at Carrington as they mulled his sacking.

Wilcox and Berrada jetted to Monaco to meet with Ineos chief Sir Jim Ratcliffe and discuss the departure of Carrick, with the club's Glazer ownership ratifying the decision to replace him with United States national team coach Pochettino.

Pochettino swapped the USA for United on Wednesday and will take charge of his first match against bitter rivals Liverpool today.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Più squadre di Serie C, sfide secche e diritti TV: ecco le due ipotesi allo studio per il futuro della Coppa Italia.

La Coppa Italia potrebbe cambiare volto nelle prossime tre stagioni. Nel nuovo bando per i diritti audiovisivi pubblicato dalla Lega Serie A, con scadenza al 14 dicembre, compaiono infatti due diverse formule pensate per rilanciare un torneo spesso snobbato fino alle fasi finali. A scegliere quale adottare sarà il mercato televisivo: prevarrà il format legato all'offerta economica più alta ricevuta dai broadcaster, con il via libera dell'Assemblea.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

La prima opzione, il Format "A", conferma l'impianto attuale della competizione con 44 squadre al via. Prevede solo 4 club di Serie C nel turno preliminare e l'ingresso delle prime otto classificate della passata Serie A direttamente dagli ottavi di finale con il vantaggio di giocare in casa. Sul piano economico, la Lega ha fissato una richiesta minima di 54 milioni di euro a stagione, pari a 162 milioni complessivi nel triennio. Una soluzione già collaudata che mantiene stabile la struttura del torneo e il relativo valore d'asta per le emittenti interessate.

Il Format "B" allargherebbe il torneo a 56 squadre, portando a 16 i club di Serie C con priorità alle Seconde Squadre (Under 23) di Serie A. Tutte partirebbero subito tranne le prime otto di Serie A (dai sedicesimi), con 24 sfide secche al primo turno, possibili incroci immediati tra A e C e l'ipotesi del sorteggio per il fattore campo. Anche le semifinali sarebbero in gara secca, aggiungendo un turno senza aumentare le gare per le finaliste, mentre le Under 23 non potrebbero affrontare le rispettive Prime Squadre se non in finale. Qui la base d'asta sale a 61 milioni annui (183 milioni nel triennio), trasformando il format in una leva commerciale per i broadcaster.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sheffield United face Southampton in the Championship tonight. The Blades come into the game in good form, having defeated Watford 4-0 on Saturday.

It has been revealed that SUFC have lost one of their last six league matches, and at Bramall Lane, they’ll be eager to give the promotion-pushing Saints a good test. However, Chris Wilder will have to undo a 17-year hoodoo to do so, and he’ll be without captain and key defender Japhet Tanganga for the tie.

Tanganga picked up his fifth booking of the season in the Watford victory and will serve his one-match suspension against Southampton. It means that 25-year-old Mark McGuinness is set to be recalled to the Sheffield United starting XI as they look for a first league point against the South Coast side since 2009.

It has been revealed that mcGuinness was touted for a move away from Bramall Lane in the summer, but he ended up staying put. He’s had a part to play at Sheffield United despite the past uncertainty too, starting seven Championship games so far this term.

According to recent reports, however, summer signing Liam Kitching has become the preferred centre-back partner for skipper Tanganga. That partnership has been increasingly impressive, providing a solid defensive foundation for SUFC to build on in their improved form of late.

But, barring a surprise call to start Jamal Baptiste for the first time since September 19th, it will be McGuinness who lines up against Southampton. The Irishman will hope his strong aerial presence and no-nonsense, box-guarding defensive style can help keep the Saints and their dangerous attackers at bay.

The likely partnership of McGuinness and Kitching will have to deal with the fit-again Cyle Larin, who scored on his return to the side against Derby County on Saturday. The Canadian international now has nine goals to his name in 14 games across all competitions this season.

Sheffield United are in for a tough task tonight, there can be no illusions over that.

Southampton have history on their side in this fixture with six consecutive league wins over the Blades since 2009. The last time SUFC were triumphant in this fixture, a late goal from Jamie Ward secured a 2-1 triumph at St Mary’s.

Industry observers note that 17 years on, the Saints are under Tonda Eckert‘s lead and pushing for Championship promotion. They sit 6th in the table, but would be 3rd if it wasn’t for their four-point deduction as part of the Spygate saga.

The visitors are the favourites, but they are not invincible away from home – far from it, in fact. Southampton have won two, drawn three and lost three of their eight league matches on the road this term, so SUFC certainly have an opening there.

McGuinness will have to step up and fill Tanganga’s shoes to deal with Larin and the rest of the Saints’ attacking threats. If they can do so, Sheffield United might just pull off an impressive win on Tuesday night.

For example, 2024 brought Paulo Fonseca with Morata, Pavlovic, Fofana, Emerson Royal, Jimenez and Abraham. Then, 2025 brought Gimenez, then Massimiliano Allegri with Modric, Rabiot, Nkunku, Jashari, and De Winter. Last summer brought Ruben Amorim with Ramos, Moreira, Gila, and Cisse.

In a recent development, A not-so-bold prediction: 2027 won’t be slow. Gerry Cardinale even hinted at this, stating: “We’ll continue to be aggressive and opportunistic. It will take a couple more transfer windows to complete everything.” The two transfer windows? Winter and summer, 2027.

According to recent reports, the Rossoneri have two key needs right now: a striker and a central defender. They’ll try to secure them as early as the month after next. Nicolo Tresoldi and Endrick are the names that have been talked about for weeks, but the transfer market has surprises.

In a recent development, the difficulties are well known: Club Brugge do not want to sell their jewel in January unless a €60m check materialises, while with Endrick it seems the will of Jose Mourinho must be taken into account. So, alternative names could emerge for the attack.

Sources indicate that A central defender is less of a pressing need. Eight months ago, Milan decided to explore the possibility of signing Virgil van Dijk, who turned 35 in July and is regarded as one of the best of his generation.

Sources indicate that A year ago, the conditions weren’t there, but now they might be. Van Dijk’s contract expires in June and he’s always been fascinated by Milan and Italy. It’s complex, but it’s worth a try, and Cardinale seems to agree.

According to recent reports, then there is Gabriele Calvani. He’s Italian, 22, plays for Frosinone, and is expected to start San Siro on Sunday. The Diavolo are interested, just as they are keen on Sporting CP’s Gonçalo Inacio, whom Amorim has already coached and attempted to sign in the summer.

Milan will undoubtedly make some changes to their bench over the next 12 months, aiming to mix young players with experienced players. Filippo Terracciano will leave in January, Vladimirov needs to play, Hutchinson is on loan until June, and Jashari will have to reconsider his future.

Recent findings suggest that it’s certain that some Diawara-like players will arrive, i.e. promising prospects chosen through scouting and data. Markus Krösche – if he becomes the new Head of Football, as is now almost certain – will have extensive powers in this regard.

The idea of ​​making the team more Italian is there, but we know how the market works, making it difficult to plan. Not only that, but some Italians will soon leave Milan too. Above all, Christian Comotto and Francesco Camarda are heading out on loan.

The former seems destined for Daniele De Rossi’s Genoa, while it remains to be seen where and under what terms the altter will leave. A loan with an option to buy, leaving Milan free to control the future, probably. To a small Serie A team? Possibly, but a move abroad is possible too.

According to recent reports, belgium and the Netherlands are countries where strikers historically have more opportunities in teams that are younger, while Germany could be another destination. If he takes a flight north, don’t be surprised.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Sources indicate that next up for Challinor and the Owls is Stevenage on Tuesday night.
  • It will be a tricky test for Sheffield Wednesday, and the key to picking up a third League One win on the trot will be keeping Boro striker Josh Magennis quiet.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that sheffield Wednesday have rediscovered winning form in League One since the arrival of Dave Challinor. The new SWFC boss oversaw a 3-0 win over Plymouth Argyle before a battling triumph at Oakwell against Barnsley.

Sources indicate that next up for Challinor and the Owls is Stevenage on Tuesday night. Boro have had an inconsistent season, leaving them in 14th as they look to build on last term’s play-off finish. Alex Revell’s side are a tough one, with physical players across the pitch.

It will be a tricky test for Sheffield Wednesday, and the key to picking up a third League One win on the trot will be keeping Boro striker Josh Magennis quiet. At 36, the Northern Irishman has been one of the standout performers at Broadhall Way this season.

Magennis moved to Stevenage in the summer after the expiry of his contract at relegated Exeter City. He maintained a consistent output with the Grecians, recording 21 goals in 89 games for the club as he plays well into his 30s.

And, he’s been a hugely effective player for Revell’s Boro too. Magennis has always been a physical presence at the top of the pitch, and the 6ft 2in striker is perfect for Stevenage. His strength and ability in the air make him a real outlet at the top of the pitch and from crossing or set-piece situations.

Recent findings suggest that not only do these attributes make him a goalscoring threat, but Magennis’ ability to win knock-downs or hold up the ball for his teammates makes him a creative asset too. If Sheffield Wednesday can’t contain him, the Bangor-born striker will be key in tonight’s game.

According to recent reports, compared with his fellow League One strikers, no one has created more goalscoring opportunities than Magennis’ 19 – six of them big chances. He wins 48% of his aerial duels and 44.4% of his duels overall (stats via FotMob).

Magennis is in some of the most productive form of his career. He is a perfect fit for Stevenage’s style of play, and it is helping him age like a fine wine and contribute in the twilight of his career.

Dealing with Magennis’ presence is not easy – his recent League One opponents will tell you that.

However, Sheffield Wednesday do have the personnel to limit his impact. In Liam Cooper, Challinor has a vastly experienced centre-back who will be wise to Magennis’ tricks and style, and he can be key in preventing the Stevenage man from having his way while guiding his fellow defenders on how to deal with him too.

According to recent reports, of the potential starters, it may be Cooper and Sil Swinkels tasked with challenging Magennis in the air. They have aerial duel win rates of 72.6% and 73.3% respectively this season, while Di’Shon Bernard has a lower but respectable 68% (FotMob).

Magennis is usually a lone striker, but with on-rushing attackers in tandem. By suffocating the Boro striker at the source, they can limit his aerial duel wins and prevent him from bringing the ball down to create chances.

It is a task easier stated than done, but SWFC boss Challinor must have a strategy to deal with Magennis if he is to maintain his perfect League One record.

Right, where were we? Three weeks on from the fifth round of Premier League fixtures in which the champions Arsenal were beaten 3-0 by Brighton and todays’ visitors, Leeds United, who remain unbeaten, drew in a tepid goalless fixture with Crystal Palace, we finally get to the sixth. As worrying as the result was at the Amex, Arsenal still created a shedload of chances and last season they were the one club that battered Leeds in both games – first early in the season when they were playing four at the back and before Dominic Calvert-Lewin, a late signing, was fully fit, and then later after they had successfully switched to a “base formation” of three centre-backs and the tactical flexibility that allowed.

It was a 5-0 tanking in August and 4-0 in January, so to say Leeds travel to a ground at which they have never won more in hope than expectation would be as true as much as it is hackneyed. Adding to a sense of foreboding and thanks to Opta’s excellent Jonny Cooper, we also have to take into account the fact that Leeds, floodlight kings, have not won a Premier League match kicking off before 3pm since August 2022 and have not won a match in London since beating Brentford in May that year to save themselves from relegation. However, they do boast the division’s best defensive record – three goals conceded – and the No1 ranked goalkeeper in James Trafford who has a save percentage of 87. For all the sense of doom, though, Leeds have become a very good side and their spine – Trafford–Muharemovic–Ampadu–Calvert-Lewin marries steel and class.

According to recent reports, arsenall need no fanfare. Until the set-back in dear old Sussex by the sea, they had looked formidable most of the time and will have been champing at the bit to get back out there and prove it was an aberration. Mikel Arteta mentioned he has doubts about Declan Rice, Kai Havertz and Ezri Konsa but Ben White, Max Dowman and Chrsthian Mosquera are all available. For Leeds Joe Rodon is still out and Dan James was injured on international duty but Harry Wilson and Jean-Matteo Bahoya returned to training after knocks this week and Daniel Farke was relatively optimistic about their prospects.

The next Lamine Yamal? Why not? Roberto De Zerbi sets high bar for Luca Williams-Barnett after 18-year-old thrilled Tottenham fans in win over Ipswich, writes MATT BARLOW
