💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 12:22 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 06:34 EST, 22 November 2026.
  • According to recent reports, luca Williams-Barnett will score better goals.
  • Roberto De Zerbi compared him to Lamine Yamal after watching the 18-year-old steal the show as Spurs beat Ipswich, their fourth win in five to move within three points of the top four.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By MATT BARLOW, FOOTBALL WRITER.

Published: 12:22 EST, 21 November 2026 | Updated: 06:34 EST, 22 November 2026.

According to recent reports, luca Williams-Barnett will score better goals. That was the consensus on a day when the Tottenham starlet marked his first Premier League by scoring the first and creating the second.

Roberto De Zerbi compared him to Lamine Yamal after watching the 18-year-old steal the show as Spurs beat Ipswich, their fourth win in five to move within three points of the top four.

'He is a special player, I am not surprised,' said De Zerbi. 'I decided 10 days ago he would play and I asked him two things. First, to play like he is on the park with his friends and then to work hard without the ball, like Raphinha and Yamal.

'In football today players with talent have to work hard and attackers are the first defenders.'.

According to recent reports, asked if Williams-Barnett could aspire to the levels of Barcelona’s Yamal, the Spurs boss replied: 'Yes, I think so'. And told how on the teenager had spent the bus ride to the stadium watching clips of Ronaldinho, Neymar and Eden Hazard on YouTube.

His goal was a picture of youthful desire and determination to get across his marker at the back post and be first to a delicious teasing cross delivered by Pedro Porro.

Roberto De Zerbi rates Williams-Barnett as ‘one of the best’ young players he has worked with.

Williams-Barnett slid and stretched past Abdoul Ouattara with his right foot as the ball skipped and hit him high on the left thigh before rebounding into the bottom corner.

In a recent development, you make your own luck. The Spurs crowd erupted. They have been waiting to hail another of their own. Maybe this is the one. A goal on his first start, just like Harry Kane, and at 18 years and 51 days, the club’s youngest league scorer since Gareth Bale.

Sources indicate that there has been a buzz growing around Williams-Barnett for the last 18 months as he rose through the academy ranks. He made his England Under-19 debut in September, coming on as a sub for Max Dowman, Arsenal’s teenage sensation.

De Zerbi adores his attitude as much as his talent, and a confidence bordering arrogance on display in pre-season when he dinked in a ‘Panenka’ style penalty in a shootout in Australia.

He is right-footed but started against Ipswich wide on the left, in the role no player has made their own since Heung-min Son.

Dominic Solanke, who scored Tottenham's second goal, congratulates his young team-mate.

Williams-Barnett might have had a second before half time, a half-chance miscued and a header saved.

Spurs fans responded. When he picked up the ball on halfway early in the second half, they roared him forward into the space ahead. He duly obliged, through the gears into a swagger and into the Ipswich penalty box without meeting a challenge.

Tottenham (4-2-3-1): Kinsky 6; Porro 7, Van Hecke 6, Senesi 6, Udogie 6 (Robertson 80); Fernandes 7, Gallagher 7; Kudus 6, Maddison 7 (Bergvall 64, 5), Williams-Barnett 8 (Savio 64, 6 (Gray 90)); Solanke 7 (Marmoush 64, 5).

Scorers: Williams-Barnett, Solanke.

Booked: Maddison, Williams-Barnett, Kudus, Fernandes.

Ipswich (3-4-2-1): Walton 7; Furlong 5, Diop 5, O’Shea 6; Outtara 4 (Fatawu 56, 5), Palacios 5 (Florentino 56, 5), Lukic 6, Davis 6 (Greaves 82); Enciso 5, Maeda 5 (Clarke 56, 5); Flemming 6.

In a recent development, belatedly, Darnell Furlong tried to hold him up. But Williams-Barnett made a yard on the outside and whipped over a cross with his left foot, which fizzed past Walton and was turned in from close range by Dominic Solanke.

The teenager booted the ball jubilantly into the crowd and collected his first yellow card from killjoy referee Rob Jones.

Williams-Barnett left to a standing ovation when he was replaced by Savio in the 64th minute. 'Luca was magnificent,' mentioned Solanke. 'To see him do that on his first Premier League start is crazy.'.

Recent findings suggest that spurs coasted in. It had been comfortable, even without some senior players including Sandro Tonali who had been unwell.

They were solid at the back and creative up front, peppering the Ipswich goal with 18 shots. Mohamed Kudus struck a post from a first-half free kick, won by Williams-Barnett.

Christian Walton made strong saves to deny James Maddison and prevent Dara O’Shea turning into his own goal.

Savio cross hit a post with a deflected cross before he was struck down by a recurrence of the hamstring injury which ruled him out for six weeks. It was the only blemish for De Zerbi, although one to enhance the opportunities ahead for Williams-Barnett.

Frosinone forward Romano Schmid believes that his side will have to be more ‘proactive’ in order to get a positive result against AC Milan.

Having been promoted from Serie B last season, Frosinone have been the surprise package so far in Serie A barring perhaps the league-leaders Lazio, as they sit sixth in the table having won six of their opening 11 games so far.

They were heavily tipped to be in a relegation battle by pundits and the bookmakers, and yet they have scored 24 goals and allowed just 15, making them not just an effective team but also an entertaining one too.

Recent findings suggest that the summer arrival Schmid – who signed from Werder Bremen – has been a part of that. He spoke at a press conference two days before Frosinone’s trip north to face Milan at San Siro. The questions and his responses were relayed by TuttoFrosinone.

After Cagliari, what will the match against Milan be like?

“The match in Milan will be completely different from the one in Cagliari. Milan are obviously the favourites, their game is different from Cagliari’s, and we’ll need a more proactive Frosinone.”.

How are you finding Serie A as a league?

According to recent reports, “It’s different from the Bundesliga, I like it. You have to always be on top of things otherwise you lose the duels, especially in midfield.”.

Did the fact that they play with a 4-2-3-1 like with Austria influence your choice to come to Frosinone?

Recent findings suggest that “It’s not the main reason. With the national team, we don’t play man-to-man like here against Frosinone. It’s a similar game because we definitely play deep, we attack high.”.

Why did you miss Austria’s last match?

“My son had a problem, it wasn’t serious but he wasn’t feeling very well and since we had already qualified I preferred to stay with the family”.

You are one of the most vital signings in Frosinone’s history, and it’s no coincidence that you started playing immediately under Alvini. How do you feel?

“My past performances in the Bundesliga were crucial; that’s one of the reasons Froisnone chose me, given my previous performances. They’re similar to what I played under coach Alvini. I’m enjoying myself and I’m happy.”.

Where do you prefer to play, in the attacking midfield role or in the pivot?

“My favourite position is number 10, an attacking midfielder behind the centre-forward. I feel comfortable playing there, I’ve also tried playing further back, but my favourite position is still number 10.”.

Industry observers note that “I haven’t played PlayStation for the last 4-5 years, since I became a father. Last night my wife downloaded the game and we played together.”.

By JAKE FENNER, US SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 09:15 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 09:15 EST, 22 November 2026.

Kansas City Current co-owner Brittany Mahomes led the celebrations as the women's soccer club won its first ever NWSL Championship on Saturday.

Brittany, the wife of Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes, was at Audi Field in Washington, DC for the final match of the season between the Current and the Washington Spirit.

A thrilling finish to the contest resulted in a 2-1 win for the Current, who have only been in existence for five years.

Brittany, who is pregnant with her fourth child, was seen on the pitch celebrating after her team's inaugural title.

She was seen embracing her team and her co-owners as they jumped up and down in celebration of the achievement.

Brittany was a part of the inaugural ownership group of the club when it was confirmed as an expansion team in 2020.

KC Current co-owner Brittany Mahomes celebrated her team winning the NWSL title.

She was seen jumping up and down and celebrating with the players as the title was clinched.

It's the first championship for the expansion club, which began playing in 2021.

Brittany's husband, Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes, also celebrated the achievement on social media.

The three-time Super Bowl champion reshared the club's announcement on X, adding, 'AHHHHHHHHHH!!!!!!!!!!' He later added, 'LETS GOOOO!!!!!!' and a string of light blue hearts.

Kansas City went ahead in the match in the 54th minute with an 'Olimpico' goal from Vanessa DiBernardo, who watched her corner kick curl to the opposite post to break a first-half deadlock.

With Washington pressing late in added time, the Current were able to score on a counter attack goal from the foot of Brazilian star Debinha to make it 2-0.

Mere seconds later, Washington's Trinity Rodman scored a goal of her own to briefly give Spirit fans hope of a miraculous comeback.

But after 11 elapsed minutes - well beyond the nine given, thanks in part to a scary collision between Rodman and KC keeper Laney Rouse - the final whistle blew as Kansas City clinched the title.

The win for the Current means yet another season of heartbreak for Washington, who have made the last three straight NWSL Championship games and have lost all three.

It has been revealed that according to a report from The Telegraph, the club have identified Icelandic manager Freyr Alexandersson as the leading candidate for their vacant head coach position. Talks have been held between the 44-year-old and the Championship club, and he appears to be their prime target at present.

Alexandersson is right now the manager of Norwegian side Rosenborg BK, who appointed him on a three-year contract in June. He has overseen 14 wins in his 19 games in charge of the club, recording a points-per-game rate of 2.32.

Alexandersson is a 44-year-old coach who has held a variety of roles in the dugout since beginning his coaching career back in 2008. He spent seven years at Leiknir Reykjavik as a player before moving into management.

The Swansea City target started out in women’s football, managing club team Valur before a short spell in charge of former club Leiknir Reykjavik. Alongside this role, Alexandersson spent five years as manager of the Iceland women’s national side.

Sources indicate that he then stepped into the men’s setup as an assistant to Erik Hamren and Arnar Vidarsson before a short spell as a No. 2 at Al-Arabi. From 2021 though, Alexandersson has worked strictly as a first-team boss in men’s football.

Recent findings suggest that he spent nearly three years in charge of Danish side Lyngby BK and 11 months at KV Kortrijk in Belgium before moving to SK Brann in Norway. Impressive work there saw him poached for the Rosenborg BK job, where he has continued to impress.

According to recent reports, swansea City head coach contender Alexandersson prioritises man management, working closely with his players to build strong relationships and placing importance on leadership. He has a strong reputation for developing players, which will appeal to the Swans too.

Tactically, his Rosenborg side set up in a 4-3-3 primarily, but he has used 5-3-2 or 3-5-2 formations in the past. Much like Matos, his teams press aggressively in the final third, and he demands frequent chance creation with players directed to suffocate opponents on and off the ball.

In terms of tactical similarities, Alexandersson feels like a great fit for Swansea City. The fact he wants his players to press high and play forwards much like Matos means that there can be a smooth transition into the upcoming management.

In a recent development, bringing in a boss with completely different ideas could bring teething problems. This squad has been built to play on the front foot with and without the ball, and Alexandersson will ensure they do so.

Sources indicate that the Jamestown Analytics influence feels clear with this pursuit. They pride themselves on finding gems in lesser-used markets, and Alexandersson could be the latest top boss uncovered.

After initial talks, time will tell whether the Swans can strike a deal to bring Alexandersson to Wales.

Further confirmation has arrived that Markus Krösche will be joining AC Milan, and an announcement could come before the month ends.

La Gazzetta dello Sport confirm the news that been circulating for weeks now: an agreement has been reached with Krösche, and next week could be the perfect time to announce it to the world, at least as per the German director and the club’s intends.

Sources indicate that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Owner Gerry Cardinale made it clear that he will never again hand the club’s management over to a single executive. He will make the decisions himself, and in the summer he chose Ruben Amorim as the head coach, working closely with him and listening closely to his transfer desires.

According to recent reports, in short, he wanted to avoid introducing the traditional role of sporting director, who at many clubs decides the coach’s fate. However, the intention to strengthen Milan’s sporting side has always been there, and Krösche has always been held in high regard by Cardinale.

Krösche officially stepped down from his role at Eintracht Frankfurt on October 18. This separation came after five and a half years of working together, with the highlight being winning the Europa League in 2021-22.

His best acquisitions were Randal Kolo Muani (bought for free after his time at Nantes and sold to PSG for €95m), Willian Pacho (bought for €13.65m from Antwerp and sold for €40m, also to PSG), and Omar Marmoush (bought for free after a year at Wolfsburg and sold to Manchester City for €70m).

Industry observers note that “Over the past few months, I’ve been intensely reflecting on my personal situation and my professional future,” Krösche stated upon his departure. “I’ve come to the conclusion that I need a change. I also believe that a fresh impetus could be helpful to Eintracht.”.

Recent findings suggest that the club recognised his great work: “Krösche has decisively shaped Eintracht Frankfurt. Winning the Europa League, participating in the Champions League, and the further growth of our team are testament to this extraordinary period.”.

Milan are his next chapter. Krösche will be responsible for transfer operations, likely taking the title of Head of Football. He will work closely with Head of Football Intelligence Bobby Gardiner and Head of Recruitment Tiago Estevão, key figures who enjoy Cardinale’s trust.

Krösche will liaise with clubs around the world and with agents. He will have a lot of responsibility, but certainly not the final say, which will rest with Cardinale after the traditional consultation with the club’s internal working group.

Above all, it will be fascinating to see what Krösche will pursue and how he will balance the pursuit of high-potential young players (his strength in Germany and a long-standing objective for Milan) with the need for short- and medium-term results.

Mane, 19, is under contract at Molineux until the summer of 2029. He has made 18 appearances for the Midlands outfit in all competitions this season, 16 of which have come in the Championship, and he has chipped in with three assists.

According to recent reports, maxwell has delivered his verdict on the youngster on the Not The Top 20 Podcast on YouTube: “Mane we hold to very high standards because we think he’s a very, very, very good player. It is always worth remembering he only turned 19 two months ago. He’s such a young player still.

“If you look at Championship minutes this season, he’s the second youngest player behind Ryan Kavuma-McQueen to have played more than 600 minutes. He’s in a little bucket there with Kavuma-McQueen, who’s still 17, then Mane and (Divine) Mukasa, who has just turned 19, and then Romelle Donovan, who is just about to turn 20.”.

Wolves will be pleased that they managed to keep hold of Mane over the summer. WWFC were relegated from the Premier League earlier this year after they finished in the bottom three along with West Ham and Burnley.

Industry observers note that mane, who is an ex-England and Portugal youth international, was linked with an exit in the last transfer window. However, nothing materialised in the end and he stayed put beyond the deadline back in early September.

Many expected the teenager to take the second tier by storm but things haven’t exactly panned out like that. He still hasn’t scored and probably hasn’t made the impact in the EFL he would have hoped to before a ball was kicked this term.

Nevertheless, he is starting to find his feet now and is a promising talent. He will get better with experience and his game is still developing.

Mane looked good against Charlton Athletic for Wolves last time out. He caused problems for WWFC’s last opponents and helped them win 2-1 after goals by Adam Armstrong and Rafiki Said.

Cesar Peixoto’s side are back in action on Tuesday night as they aim to keep their momentum going. They face another match on their own patch against Derby County.

In a recent development, the Rams are in poor form and are in the drop zone along with Burnley and Preston North End. They have won only twice in the league and are five points from safety behind both Lincoln City and Watford after their 2-0 loss at Southampton over the weekend.

According to recent reports, wolves will fancy their chances of securing another win to boost their promotion push as they chase down the top two Middlesbrough and Stoke City. They are presently sat in 3rd place in the table after 16 fixtures and they are in the play-offs along with Birmingham City, West Brom, Southampton, QPR and Swansea City.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In the past few weeks, Ruben Amorim has been battling a long list of absences due to injuries, but how does it compare to one year ago?
  • The second international break brings a useful moment to pause and reflect on the injury problems within the squad.
  • Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In the past few weeks, Ruben Amorim has been battling a long list of absences due to injuries, but how does it compare to one year ago?

The second international break brings a useful moment to pause and reflect on the injury problems within the squad. Given that there have been at times as many as eight players out, it feels as though Amorim has been rowing against the tide a bit.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The Portuguese asks for a physically demanding style and he consistently emphasises the importance of proper rotation. Yet, at present, the likes of Matteo Gabbia, Samuel Chukwueze, Fikayo Tomori, Ruben Loftus-Cheek, Alexis Saelemaekers and Strahinja Pavlovic are all out.

From Stefano Pioli’s final years into Massimiliano Allegri’s one-season stint, there was a recurring problem of muscle complications. For example, last season – despite no European football – the Rossoneri suffered 31 total injuries during the season, leading to a crisis at certain points.

In the previous season, which included the Champions League, the figure hit 33. In Pioli’s last season in 2023-24, he battled a staggering 40 different problems. How does the current season compare to the last though? MilanNews provide the data.

1. Pulisic – Ankle sprain – July 26 to August 12, 17 days out during the summer. 2. Leao – Right calf elongational injury – August 17 to September 25, 39 days out and missed 5 games. 3. Jashari – Compound fracture of the right fibula – August 28 to October 30, 63 days out. 9 games missed so far. 4. Pavlovic – Flexor problem – from September 14 to September 18, 4 days out. 5. Maignan – Right calf problem – from September 14 to September 23, 9 days out and 1 game missed. 6. Tomori – Right aductor strain – from September 28 to October 3, 5 days out. 7. Saelemaekers – Right flexor injury – from October 11 to October 18, 7 days out. 8. Estupinan – Ankle problem – from October 11 to October 30, 19 days out and 3 games missed. 9. Pulisic – Right thigh hamstring injury – from October 11 to November 5, 25 days out and 4 games missed. 10. Rabiot – Left soleus injury – from October 16 to November 18, 33 days out and 5 games missed. 11. Loftus-Cheek – Muscle strain – October 18 to October 27, 9 days out and 2 games missed. 12. Nkunku – Toe problem – October 16 to October 23, 7 days out and 1 game missed. 13. Leao – Hip problem – October 28 to October 30, 2 days out. 14. Tomori – Knee problem – October 28 to November 1, 4 days out. 15. Gimenez – Ankle problem and arthroscopic surgery – October 28, 2025 to March 21, 2026, 114 days out and 22 games missed.

Total: Seven traumatic/other and eight muscular in 13 matches played (11 Serie A, 2 Coppa Italia).

1. Pulisic – Bone edema at the junction of the tibia and fibula, July 8 to August 21. 44 days out during preseason. 2. Gila – Right rectus femoris strain, July 25 to August 12. 18 days out during preseason. 3. Gabbia – Ankle problems, September 1 to 11. 10 days out and missed 1 game. 4. Saelemaekers – Right ankle problem and subsequent surgery, since September 29. 5. Gabbia – Left thigh flexor injury, with partial tendon involvement, since October 11. 6. Chukwueze – Left hip tensor fascia latae tendon rupture, resulting in surgery, since October 21. 7. Ramos – Calf muscle overload, October 21 to 23. 2 days out and missed 1 game. 8. Gila – Overuse inflammation in the left ankle, from October 24 to 29. 5 days out and missed 2 games. 9. Rabiot – Right calf strain, from October 24 to 29. 5 days out and missed 2 games. 10. Moreira – Left calf flexor strain, from October 24 to 29. 5 days out and missed 2 games. 11. Loftus-Cheek – Left medial flexor injury, from October 25. 12. Tomori – Right medial flexor injury, from October 29. 13. Pavlovic – Renal colic, from November 4 to 17. 13 days out and missed 2 games.

Total: Five traumatic/other and eight muscular from 15 matches played (11 Serie A, 4 Europa League).

In a recent development, so, while things might have felt quite bleak at various moments when gazing into a packed treatment room, Amorim has actually had a bit more luck than his predecessor when it comes to physical concerns. Now he must hope that continues, or even that he gets luckier still.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Millwall have struggled to replicate the form of last term which saw them finish in 3rd place. They presently languish in 16th place following three consecutive Championship defeats.

Injuries have plagued the Lions’ early-season endeavours, and a run of two victories in 10 outings, coming against lowly Preston North End and Derby County, has left supporters debating whether Alex Neil is the right man to take them forward.

It has been revealed that there is no shame in falling to Birmingham City and West Brom, despite poor performances against the two promotion contenders. However, the Lions’ loss to QPR escalated the cause for concern when they were played off the park, not helped by Zak Sturge’s early dismissal.

Stoke City meanwhile are 2nd in the table after four consecutive wins. They defeated Birmingham City on Saturday despite playing much of the second half with 10 men after Luca Bombino’s sending off.

Sturge will serve his one-game suspension against Stoke City after denying a clear goal-scoring opportunity by pulling down QPR forward Paul Smyth.

In a recent development, the absences of Millwall duo Ryan Leonard and Tristan Crama have been felt in the backline, with the latter struggling with ongoing ankle problems while Leonard has been sidelined with a knee injury. Both are expected to make a return at the start of December.

A similar return timeframe is in the pipeline for Filip Marschall, who suffered an ankle ligament injury in their draw to Lincoln City in October.

Recent findings suggest that mathis Servais was among a number of Millwall’s summer arrivals who generated considerable excitement upon arrival, signing from Belgian outfit KV Mechelen. He has played just nine minutes of Championship football due to a hamstring injury and remains out here.

Jensen; Sykes, Taylor, Cooper, Doughty; De Norre, Metcalfe; Neghli, Arconte, Lisbie; Ivanovic.

Jensen started his first game in goal for the first time in two months against QPR, and the injury to Marschall means he has hold of the number one shirt ahead of Max Crocombe.

In a recent development, caleb Taylor and Jake Cooper have been Neil’s go-to centre-back pairing this term, starting in all 16 Championship matches, and will likely continue their partnership with Mark Sykes set to start at right-back. The red card to Sturge means the left-back role is up for grabs, one which Alfie Doughty could fill against his former side with Jordi Osei-Tutu also another option.

Casper de Norre was withdrawn at half-time against QPR but should be fit to start alongside Jenson Metcalfe.

Promising wideman Kyrell Lisbie has been deployed on both flanks of the attack this term and will likely start on the left, with Camiel Neghli occupying the right as he looks to rediscover the form he indicated last season.

Kyrell Lisbie’s Championship stats.

Yet to score since drawing with Middlesbrough in September, Tairyk Arconte will look to rediscover his finishing touch as the Guadeloupe international looks set to line up in an advanced midfield role.

It has been revealed that the responsibility of leading the line has fallen to Lyndon Dykes this term, but he has been part of a misfiring Millwall attack. As such, Serbian striker Mihailo Ivanovic could come in his place for only his second league start of the season.

Stoke City vs Millwall kicks off at 20:00 at the Bet365 Stadium and will be broadcast live on Sky Sports Main Event and Sky Sports Football.

#84058. Breaking: Man Utd make worst start in 40 years after being hauled back by 10-man Spurs

Breaking: Man Utd make worst start in 40 years after being hauled back by 10-man Spurs

📅 10 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 21 min read (4264 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~21 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Manchester United fans were never going to pass up the opportunity to aim a volley of abuse in the direction of their bitter rivals.
  • By the end of another deeply unconvincing performance, though, they were more preoccupied by the problems afflicting their own team than the cheating scandal engulfing Manchester City.
  • Against City at Old Trafford last month, United lost to a team who were down to 10 men after just 23 minutes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester United fans were never going to pass up the opportunity to aim a volley of abuse in the direction of their bitter rivals.

By the end of another deeply unconvincing performance, though, they were more preoccupied by the problems afflicting their own team than the cheating scandal engulfing Manchester City.

Against City at Old Trafford last month, United lost to a team who were down to 10 men after just 23 minutes.

This time around they could not hold on to a lead against a Tottenham Hotspur side also navigating a numerical disadvantage following Rodrigo Bentancur’s sending off.

Industry observers note that rodrigo Bentancur dives in on Luke Shaw and it's all kicking off at Old Trafford! 🫨 https://t.co/uJUAMuZNzc.

The sum total of it all is that United have now made their worst start to a season for 40 years, which is saying something given the traumas of the post-Ferguson era, and perhaps more disconcertingly, look to all intents and purposes like a team going backwards.

The bounce they enjoyed under Michael Carrick last season en route to Champions League qualification is over and, after just six points from as many games, it is hard to shake the feeling that it is going to be anything but a serious battle to finish in the top four or five.

Recent findings suggest that the supporters did not hide their disgruntlement. There were boos around the half hour mark after an insipid opening when Spurs did everything but score and a slow, sluggish, dishevelled United almost looked impervious to their troubles.

Carrick had called for his players to show some “fire” coming into this match, but instead watched them ambling around like it was all a terrible inconvenience. The ease with which Spurs ran around them was alarming. There were more jeers at the interval and again at full time.

Carrick admitted that “hurt” although not as much you suspect as the sight of players feigning interest and then throwing away three points when they had finally summoned some fight to lead courtesy of Bryan Mbeumo’s goal.

Recent findings suggest that bryan Mbeumo slots it home to give Manchester United the lead against Spurs! 🎯 https://t.co/7yKnpyhfUe.

Recent findings suggest that it was a lovely finish after good work by the largely anonymous Matheus Cunha, and when Bentancur was sent off five minutes later after butting Luke Shaw, it should have been the cue to see out the game. To fail to do so against a side as toothless as Tottenham made it all the worse. Leading late on against Everton last month, they also failed to get over the line. It cannot keep happening.

Equally, United cannot play like they did in the first half here when they face Atlético Madrid in the Spanish capital on Tuesday night or at Elland Road against bitter rivals Leeds five days later and expect to get anything from either game. They are not the sort of matches Carrick would want with his team in this shape, but they need to find some inspiration from somewhere.

Carlos Baleba coming on around the hour mark and making a difference on his debut will at least offer Carrick some grounds for encouragement. The £65m midfield signing from Brighton offers some energy and urgency and looks a more natural bedfellow for Kobbie Mainoo than Youri Tielemans, who was woeful against Spurs and should have come off earlier.

In a recent development, in truth, Tielemans was not alone. Throughout the team there was a disconnect and unease and Carrick admitted it became contagious.

Recent findings suggest that “We just couldn’t find a way to get ourselves into the game, whether that was with the ball or without the ball,” the United manager noted. “We were a little bit slow with the decision-making, didn’t quite see the passing areas, the space. You don’t want it to happen, but sometimes it can and it probably spread through the team a little bit too much.”.

Recent findings suggest that it does not help that Bruno Fernandes is being hampered by an injury he has been carrying for weeks or that Carrick has no natural centre-forward to call upon with Benjamin Sesko again sidelined by the recurrence of a worrying shin problem. Amad Diallo did return here after a lengthy lay-off of his own, but did not look match fit.

In defence, Lisandro Martínez did enough to put off Dominic Solanke, who fired over from Sávio’s cross in the second half, but this was otherwise another poor showing from the Argentine centre-back, one of several positions where United need upgrades.

United needed shaking badly, but when Carrick turned to his bench he called upon Joshua Zirkzee, a fitful forward the club wanted to sell this summer, and right-back Diogo Dalot in addition to Baleba.

Marcus Rashford cannot have been fit given he was only introduced in the 95th minute and perhaps the same was true of the unused Mason Mount. As for £50m summer signing Andrey Santos, this was another league game when the Brazilian midfielder did not get a look in.

Industry observers note that united fans had taunted Spurs when a goal and a man up. “You’re going down with the City,” they crowed, a nod to the possibility of City being expelled or relegated from the Premier League after being found guilty of breaching more than 100 financial rules.

Recent findings suggest that united fans had also revived their Stretford End “ticker” after reaching the conclusion that none of City’s titles under Abu Dhabi ownership had been won fairly so, in their eyes, it is now 50 years since their rivals last won anything legitimately. City, of course, continue to maintain their innocence and have lodged an appeal.

But United fans were unable to crow for too long once Solanke levelled.

Industry observers note that spurs are level in stoppage-time! 😳 https://t.co/NoivNchgWw.

Recent findings suggest that it had been similar early in the game when the home fans had trained their sights on City. “You cheating b--------, you know what you are”, they sang lustily.

But as the match wore on, those chants began to quieten as the crowd, taking their lead from the team, fell decidedly flat.

Carrick is going to have to find a spark from somewhere and swiftly.

Speaking to BBC Match of the Day, Carrick said: “It was a mixed game. We found it tough to start with. For a number of reasons, we were not quite there. You could see it was a challenging time.

It has been revealed that “But the lads grew into the game, in the second half I thought we were better in everything. To get the game as we wanted it, in such a good position - we should see it through. We have to manage those situations. That’s two late goals which have hurt us, and things look very different. That’s the reality.”.

When asked about the boos at half-time and full-time, he replied: “It’s not nice, it hurts a lot because I care about this club. But I understand the disappointment, the reality is what it is, we need to get back to winning games.”.

3 - Manchester United have failed to win any of their last three Premier League games against sides that have received a red card (D1 L2). Disadvantage? https://t.co/DuSpvymZfu.

The Tottenham boss told Sky Sports: “I think we played very well against a great team. We had many chances to score in the first half. Three or four. The second half is normal to suffer against this quality. I am very happy because I have seen the right spirit and character.

It has been revealed that “We suffered in the game but every situation of the game. I like the situation we were in with the red card. We need this situation. We have not accepted the defeat. We have to react in all ways we can. It is a bad way, it is not the right way. I kiss Bentancur in the dressing room. Football is character.

In a recent development, “We win the game if we play as a team. We didn’t win this game playing as a team. Every game like today, we will win many games.”.

When asked about Solanke, he replied: “He is a good player for Tottenham. There for not too many strikers better than Solanke. Today he was captain because he deserved it, especially in this moment because he suffer because Tottenham didn’t score or win any games. He is a great guy, great player and we are behind him.

Industry observers note that “We have to believe in ourselves and this football way. If we believe, improve and play as a team, we will score many goals and win many games. If we don’t play as a team, it is impossible.”.

"Today we demonstrated so much fight and grit!" Dominic Solanke on Spurs' mentality to rescue a point at Old Trafford 💪 https://t.co/jurK07E6jU.

"They look devoid of any confidence" Jamie Redknapp says Manchester United's squad is not strong enough ❌ https://t.co/oZgmtWelJB.

"They were the better team today by far" Gary Neville reacts at full-time as Spurs grab a late equaliser at Manchester United 💬 https://t.co/T37kkDy5uj.

It has been revealed that more jeers at the final whistle from United fans - they weren’t happy with this point against a team there for the taking after Rodrigo Bentancur’s dismissal. Michael Carrick is still trying to find answers because this United team is not clicking.

In a recent development, the late chaos is over at Old Trafford as Solanke rescues a precious point for Tottenham with that 92nd minute equaliser. Man Utd thought they had the game wrapped up after Mbeumo’s well-taken opener was followed by Bentancur’s crazy red card. However, Spurs, who were the better team throughout the contest, kept fighting and found a fully deserved leveller. The visitors remain winless, but it’s another worrying performance from Carrick’s side, who have picked up just one victory in six top-flight matches.

A point apiece in Manchester. https://t.co/xiEiQsFsje.

Dalot and Gray are both handed yellow cards for fouls that broke up play. Despite their numerical disadvantage, Spurs right now look like the more likely side to claim a victory.

In a recent development, it’s just the Spurs fans singing in Old Trafford now. They fully deserved that equaliser. Rashford and Heaven are on for the hosts, with Cunha and Shaw taken off.

Incredible drama at Old Trafford! Tonali floats a cross into the box and Solanke shrugs off Martinez, before flicking a delicate header into the bottom corner to send Spurs’ away support wild. Man Utd are stunned. Could the visitors go on and win this now?

Recent findings suggest that spurs are level in stoppage-time! 😳 https://t.co/NoivNchgWw.

Van Hecke does well to block Cunha’s effort and the referee indicates that there will be a minimum of eight minutes of added time.

Sources indicate that de Zerbi’s final roll of the dice in search of a late leveller sees Fernandes replace Senesi for the remaining few minutes. Spurs must throw everyone forward now.

Martinez lunges in on Maddison and brings down the playmaker with a foul. The centre-back picks up a yellow card for his troubles.

In a recent development, baleba unleashes Mbeumo with an over-the-top through ball. Racing through on goal, the forward shoots, but from an unfavourable angle, Kinsky parries his near post effort out for a corner.

Fernandes is cautioned after catching Van Hecke with a late challenge on his ankle. Spurs players aren’t happy with the tackle.

Bentancur’s recklessness has left Spurs with a mountain to climb. Their chance of a comeback looks a bit slimmer now that Man Utd have a numerical advantage on the pitch.

It’s all kicked off at Old Trafford! Bentancur flies in with a risky challenge on Shaw. The Man Utd defender is furious with the tackle and the two players square up to each other. Shaw pushes Bentancur over and the midfielder responds by leaning into the Englishman, creating a headbutt-like action. Shaw and Van Hecke are also given yellows for their roles in that altercation.

In a recent development, rodrigo Bentancur dives in on Luke Shaw and it's all kicking off at Old Trafford! 🫨 https://t.co/uJUAMuZNzc.

Rodrigo Bentancur is sent off... and here's why ⬇️ https://t.co/3ahzz5iUbg.

Spurs respond to going behind by making a double change as Van de Ven and Maddison come on to replace Udogie and Gallagher.

According to recent reports, it’s against the run of play, but Man Utd won’t care, they have the all-crucial advantage! Cunha runs into a channel and slips a pass into Mbeumo. Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this mouthwatering Premier League game between Manchester United and Tottenham at Old Trafford.

If Manchester City had not entered a legal battle with the Premier League after being found guilty of breaching 114 charges relating to financial regulations by an independent panel, then surely there would be more pressure on the two head coaches in the dugout this evening?

Man Utd and Tottenham have undoubtedly both endured extremely disappointing starts to their respective top-flight campaigns. The hosts sit just inside the bottom half of the table after picking up just five points from their opening five matches. It’s going even worse for Tottenham, who languish in 20th with zero wins and just two points.

The perilous landscape leaves only one reasonable conclusion: this has all the ingredients for an early season six-pointer.

The strain is perhaps less intense on Michael Carrick, with the Englishman having built up a bundle of goodwill after cleaning up the mess left by Ruben Amorim last season as Man Utd eventually finished third, qualifying for the Champions League. Fans were left slightly underwhelmed by the club’s transfer window, with the players at Carrick’s disposal having not forged any momentum so far in this campaign.

The spotlight is definitely shining more intensely upon Roberto De Zerbi after substantial-spending Tottenham splashed over £300m in the summer on the likes of Sandro Tonali, Mateus Fernandes, Jan Paul van Hecke and Savio. However, the Italian boss is yet to strike the correct rhythm with his newly-formed squad. An encouraging performance backed up by a positive result here at Old Trafford could be the perfect antidote to ease the worries of fans fearing that Tottenham could be embroiled in another relegation battle.

Alphadjo Cisse has definitely been the breakout player of the season so far and Ruben Amorim has no intention of dialling down his presence in attack.

According to recent reports, milan had a very clear plan when they headed into the current season: Goncalo Ramos would be the main man in attack. Instead, however, it’s the underdog Cisse who has been running the show, while the Portuguese striker has been at the bottom in terms of output.

According to recent reports, read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

As highlighted by Gazzetta dello Sport this morning (see image below), that’s why there cannot be – and likely won’t be – a Milan without Cisse in attack. Ruben Amorim now wants to build the attack around him, as opposed to introducing him every now and then.

Recent findings suggest that the most recent clash, the 2-1 win against Genoa, was a good example of this. Amorim went for a bold formation with Cisse, Ramos, Christian Pulisic, Diego Moreira, Luka Modric and Adrien Rabiot together. A team with a lot of quality and an attacking-minded style.

It has been revealed that it was a shape that reminded us of 2009-10, when Milan were guided by another foreign coach: Leonardo. He chose a very attacking-minded side with four attackers and two midfielders, which is something that Amorim almost replicated.

Modric and Rabiot in front of the defence (Pirlo and Ambrosini then) and the fantasy project with Pulisic, Moreira, Cisse, and Ramos, comparable to the Ronaldinho, Pato, Seedorf, and Borriello of the old days.

Despite this, the goals were scored after two mistakes by Genoa (even if Milan’s pressing helped), so the goal is to repeat the experiment against Frosinone and to increase its effectiveness, the experiment should be repeated tomorrow.

According to recent reports, in that sense, Cisse will be vital as he’s the top scorer: three goals in Europa League and five in Serie A. He has scored with both feet and his head, demonstrating a combination of talent and an eye for goal: characteristics that are very important for a team like Milan.

The average also speaks for itself: eight goals spread across 658 minutes means he scores a goal every 82 minutes. Best of all, his versatility means that he can play as an attacking midfielder, a left-winger, and even as a centre-forward.

According to recent reports, at just 20 years and 17 days old, thanks to the fifth goal in his ninth Serie A appearance, Cisse became the second-youngest player to reach the milestone in the first ten games with Milan, at least since 1994-95. Only Pato did it younger, at 18 years and 181 days.

Furthermore, he’s one of only three players born after 2006 (top five leagues) to have scored eight or more goals in all competitions, along with Lamine Yamal (13) and Paris Brunner, who also scored eight.

As the pink newspaper concludes, Ramos has also produced eye-catching numbers, but in this case in a negative sense: 1,191 minutes on the pitch, three goals scored, meaning one goal scored every 398 minutes.

Pochettino needs to change things swiftly, very quickly.

That is the chant that will be going through Andoni Iraola's head tonight; he just loves playing Manchester United.

The only manager to record a longer unbeaten run against the Red Devils in the competition is one of his predecessors, Jurgen Klopp (eight between 2018 and 2022).

Liverpool certainly picked the right man for this rivalry.

Sources indicate that watford swiftly turned their attention to Edward Iordanescu after parting ways with Alessio Dionisi on Sunday. The Hornets sacked the Italian following a 4-0 defeat against Sheffield United.

Yesterday, it was reported that Iordanescu had verbally agreed to become the newly introduced head coach at Vicarage Road, with the hope that he could take charge of Wednesday’s fixture against Blackburn Rovers. However, a new update from Sky Sports’ Anthony Joseph states that the Romanian is still in talks over his contract length and has not travelled to England yet.

Recent findings suggest that the club remain hopeful of sealing the deal despite the setback. Iordanescu has been out of management since October 2025, when he departed Legia Warsaw.

It has been revealed that he has mostly managed in his homeland, alongside spells in Poland and Bulgaria. A move to England would be the first in his career, should it be completed.

Watford have lost three of their last six matches, with their last defeat against Sheffield United. Although their defensive vulnerabilities stood out against the Blades, their attacking weaknesses have been more evident this season.

Clubs including Burnley, Bolton and Cardiff City have conceded more than Watford this season, while 16 teams have conceded less.

The Hornets are currently the lowest scorers in the Championship with 13 goals. Amin Nabizada is the club’s leading scorer with three goals, ahead of Myron Boadu on two. Furthermore, Watford have failed to score in seven matches so far this season. They also rank 19th in shots per match this season, highlighting the lack of creativity in the side.

According to recent reports, as a coach, Iordanescu’s philosophies place an emphasis on defensive organisation. This could help Watford, but they need to improve in the attacking department more.

The Romanian manager, should he join Watford, would bring international pedigree and trophies from his homeland.

However, Iordanescu has been at nine clubs in fifteen years, so he isn’t exactly a boss to build a long-term dynasty. He is yet to manage in England as well, which marks a risk in a likely Championship relegation fight.

Burnley opted for Fabio Celestini in their managerial search, another boss without English experience, and he is yet to turn his side’s form around.

Iordanescu would have the January transfer window around the corner to shape the squad to his liking. His impact will need to be immediate, as concerns grow at Vicarage Road.

  • According to recent reports, ever since the summer, when the BBC were the first to report on Milan’s interest, Fernandes has been brought up by various outlets as an option for the Rossoneri.
  • Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bruno Fernandes has ended up on AC Milan’s radar ahead of the summer, according to reports, with a free transfer potentially on the cards.

According to recent reports, ever since the summer, when the BBC were the first to report on Milan’s interest, Fernandes has been brought up by various outlets as an option for the Rossoneri. Just a few days ago, Fabrizio Romano mentioned he is ‘more than a dream’ for them and that Ruben Amorim could be key.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Having just turned 32, Fernandes is still at a good age and he’s showing that with Manchester United so far this season. In 14 appearances, he has bagged six goals and three assists, so it’s no surprise that many clubs are monitoring his situation given the expiring contract.

Sources indicate that as reported by both Corriere dello Sport (via MilanNews) and Tuttosport (via MilanNews) this morning, Milan are seriously evaluating the idea of signing him. It’s still too early to talk about negotiations, but he’s definitely on their radar and will likely remain there.

Of course, if he does end up leaving on a free transfer, there will be no shortage of suitors so Milan would likely have to table a hefty contract offer. The club owner, Gerry Cardinale, seems more willing to do that now, though, than he did just a year ago.

According to recent reports, one potential problem is that Manchester United have confirmed that they are discussing a renewal with the player. The CEO Omar Berrada showered the Portuguese star with praise, as cited by Fabrizio Romano, so it seems a stay in Manchester cannot be ruled out either.

Key midfielder set for assessment as latest Blackburn Rovers injury revision emerges for Watford test

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (552 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Blackburn Rovers’ key midfielder Sam Morsy was absent from their 2-2 draw with Burnley after sustaining a knock in training.
  • The experienced Egyptian has been an ever-present in Rovers’ side this term since signing in the summer.
  • Recent findings suggest that meanwhile, Tom Atcheson is under concussion protocols after coming off early against Burnley, following a hit to the head.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Blackburn Rovers’ key midfielder Sam Morsy was absent from their 2-2 draw with Burnley after sustaining a knock in training. However, he is aiming to return to Championship action on Wednesday night against a managerless Watford.

The experienced Egyptian has been an ever-present in Rovers’ side this term since signing in the summer. Morsy has featured on 14 occasions in the league, but is facing a race to be fit in time. On his fitness, caretaker boss Damien Johnson told the Lancashire Telegraph: “Sam was touch and go for the weekend and is similar. He is still being assessed this morning. We will have more news on that after training.”.

Recent findings suggest that meanwhile, Tom Atcheson is under concussion protocols after coming off early against Burnley, following a hit to the head. The academy graduate has also been a regular feature with his impressive performances at the heart of defence seeing him keep his place in the Northern Ireland national team.

Industry observers note that blackburn Rovers have been spearheaded by the sensational form of Andri Gudjohnsen, who is only behind Will Lankshear in the goalscoring charts with 11 to his name. But, it has been a collective effort to see them sit in 13th place.

Rovers were showing signs of real promise prior to Tony Mowbray stepping away from the dugout, most notably an impressive 2-1 victory over West Ham before the international break, with Morsy and Atcheson firmly part of that.

Morsy has filled the role as the anchor of Rovers’ midfield admirably and has shown his worth as one of the Championship’s finest midfield operators at 35.

Atcheson meanwhile is at the opposite end of his career, but has been just as influential. He usually plays on the right-hand side of the back three and impresses with his desire to orchestrate attacks from deep.

Both Morsy and Atcheson are vital cogs in Blackburn’s machine and they will be desperate to have the pair available for a favourable-looking encounter against a troubled Watford side.

Hoping to close the gap to the play-off places to just two points with a victory, Blackburn will certainly fancy their chances with the opponents registering a solitary victory in their last five outings.

Morsy’s experience has been vital for midfield partner Kristi Montgomery who is enjoying his breakout campaign at Ewood Park, and his quality on the ball is still there for all to see at 36.

Nonetheless, Moussa Baradji stepped up to fill his shoes last time out, while Gady Beyuku also strengthened his case for a starting berth in place of Atcheson so Johnson has a wealth of options should either of his key players be unavailable.

AC Milan are thinking about bolstering their academy with the Malmö FF talent Leon Da Silva, according to a report.

In recent months, a lot of focus has been on how Milan will reinforce the first team in January and next summer. Understandably so, as Gerry Cardinale seemingly has big spending plans, keen on making it back to the Champions League next season.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Amidst all of the first-team rumours, however, Milan are also working on the academy. Jovan Kirovski is evaluating players for the Futuro side with his team, while Vincenzo Vergine (pictured) and his team are doing so for the Primavera and below.

According to Gianluca Di Marzio, one of the players on Milan’s wish list is Leon Da Silva, who currently plays in the academy of Malmö FF. At the age of 16, he’s yet to make his debut with the first team, but he did feature in a friendly game last month.

Industry observers note that da Silva plays as a centre-back and as the report states, he has even been compared to Virgil Van Dijk for how he plays. Since he’s still very young, if Milan were to secure his services, he would start with the Primavera team (or even in the younger sides).

In addition to Milan, the likes of Inter and Torino are also monitoring the Swede, though it seems Malmö are keen on keeping him for a few more years.

Freyr Alexandersson emerges as contender for Swansea City job in surprise twist

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Swansea City's hunt for an heir to Vitor Matos has now taken another twist, with the Welsh outfit having set their sights on former Iceland women's head coach Freyr Alexandersson.
  • Swansea were rocked by the news of the departure of former head coach Vitor Matos last week, with the former Liverpool and RB Salzburg coach choosing to head to France and link up with Chelsea-affiliated BlueCo outfit Strasbourg.
  • As a result, a coaching team consisting of Ashley Williams, Leon Britton, and Joe Allen have taken charge of things in Swansea for now as the hunt for Matos' replacement continues, as a surprise newly introduced contender has emerged.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Swansea City's hunt for an heir to Vitor Matos has now taken another twist, with the Welsh outfit having set their sights on former Iceland women's head coach Freyr Alexandersson.

Swansea were rocked by the news of the departure of former head coach Vitor Matos last week, with the former Liverpool and RB Salzburg coach choosing to head to France and link up with Chelsea-affiliated BlueCo outfit Strasbourg.

As a result, a coaching team consisting of Ashley Williams, Leon Britton, and Joe Allen have taken charge of things in Swansea for now as the hunt for Matos' replacement continues, as a surprise newly introduced contender has emerged.

According to The Telegraph's Mike McGrath, Icelandic coach Freyr Alexandersson has emerged as the leading contender for the vacant role at the Swansea.com Stadium, having held talks with the club.

Alexandersson, 44, began his coaching career aged just 26, assisting Valur's women's team in his native Iceland, before spells with Leiknir Reykjavík, Iceland women's national team, Iceland men's national team, Al-Arabi, Lyngby, Kortrijk, SK Brann, and now Rosenborg followed.

Swansea have a partnership with Jamestown Analytics, the same model that Brighton and Hove Albion use to recruit players and staff, and that system has likely played a part in the sounding out of Alexandersson.

The current Rosenborg boss has his side sitting in 4th in the Norwegian Eliteserien as things stand, some 18 points behind league leader Bodo/Glimt, as Swansea are trusting their data with this potential appointment.

Unsurprisingly, Swansea were not entirely pleased with the swift departure of Matos, as with Strasbourg's interest emerging, a deal that saw the former Jürgen Klopp understudy head to France was done barely 48 hours later.

Swansea have received a compensation fee in excess of £5 million for Matos, though having been allowed to build the team in his image and get them flying towards the top of the league, it's not the end of the relationship either party surely would've hoped for.

In a statement released by Swansea, the club barely touched on Matos' exit, saying: "Per RC Strasbourg's announcement, Swansea City acknowledges that Vitor Matos and his coaching staff have left the club.".

Now, the hunt for a replacement continues, with Alexandersson emerging from nowhere to go into pole position for the role, as the Welsh outfit looks to maintain their push for promotion in a upcoming era.

What do you make of this potential appointment? Who would you like to see replace Vitor Matos at Swansea? Share your thoughts below!

With Williams and a bunch of Swansea favourites over the years taking the helm for now, the club will hope they can remain in contention for automatic promotion moving forward after this jarring and unexpected period.

Whether Alexandersson will be the correct person to take the club forward remains to be seen, as Swansea are putting their faith in Jamestown Analytics and leaning into the data model fully for this potential appointment.

Time will tell how this one plays out, as Swansea fans won't care who is in charge as long as they can maintain their push towards the top of the Championship and forget all about Matos in due course.
